One of Sagat's strongest midrange options due to its long range, solid damage, Target Combo follow-up, and low crush potential.

During startup, Sagat's hurtbox moves forward only a tiny distance and does not extend a leg hurtbox until the active frames, making it essentially unchallengeable at mid range. The hitbox itself is disjointed, capable of cleanly stuffing most counterpokes when spaced near max range. The leg hurtbox is raised so high that it dodges not only low pokes, but crouching buttons like Cammy's 2MP as well. The only real way to contest it is with projectiles or predictive jumps/ Drive Impact , though if the opponent manages to make it whiff it's possible to score a whiff punish with a longer range button like a Sweep or 2MK .

While not the most effective Drive Rush starter, its hurtbox properties can cause the opponent's DR check to whiff completely, letting Sagat hit for a Punish Counter with massive frame advantage ( +11 ). Your follow-up is heavily range-dependent, with 2HK or another 5MK being the most consistent links.

The Middle Step Kick follow-up TC is borderline hitconfirmable depending on your reaction speed. If you're not confident reacting, it still works well as a whiff punish tool to score a knockdown.

Furthest horizontal distance; much better block advantage when spaced at max range; 2nd hit active frames 1-9 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out so the first hit whiffs, it connects on the 2nd to last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+4 on block); if the 1st hit is crouch blocked, opponent cannot switch to stand block the 2nd hit; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP if the last 6 active frames connect, or 623MP / SA2 if the final active frame connects); blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; Sweet Spot occurs when juggling into the 3rd or 4th active frame, dealing 1300 damage (single hit) with a higher spinning juggle launch (ensures a follow-up juggle is possible even midscreen); the 2nd hit's extended Knee hitbox is too high to connect on standing characters on active frames 2-7 (tall characters: active frames 4-6); sets up corner safe jump in certain juggle scenarios (e.g. after juggled 2MP~HP)

236KK 236XX or A[5S]

OD Tiger Knee Crush

1st hit transitions to a different follow-up on hit, resulting in higher damage and a tumbling +66 knockdown (allows a 623LP juggle in the corner); if 1st hit whiffs, the next 2 hits deal 500 damage each and give a worse knockdown (only 1 hit at farthest ranges); safe on block but usually lands inside the opponent's throw range; 2nd hit active frames 2-10 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out, it connects on the last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+1 on block); unlike HK Knee, the opponent can switch to stand block after the first hit connects, leaving Sagat at -2; blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; later hits put opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP)

1f extra recovery vs. armor (DI is a guaranteed punish if not canceled to SA3); the only strength of 214K that can combo naturally from 5LP (3-light confirm can reach if point blank, but results in weaker mixup from ~6LK ender); does not frame trap when canceled on block (except from Light normals with Drive Rush or Burnout); combos into 6LK/6MK follow-ups; canceling into the 6HK follow-up leaves a 2f gap on hit / 9f gap on block (loses to 4f normals even in Burnout); Counter-hit/Punish Counter puts the opponent into a limited juggle state that allows the 6HK follow-up to combo; cannot perform follow-up attacks on whiff; opponents can beat all follow-ups with invincible reversals (but standard 6f reversals will not punish 214LK); if the opponent attempts to punish 214LK, the 6LK follow-up will frame trap on block (must delay 6LK vs. Burnout)

1f extra recovery vs. armor (DI is a guaranteed punish if not canceled to SA3); combos into 6LK/6MK follow-ups; canceling into the 6HK follow-up leaves a 2f gap on hit / 9f gap on block (loses to 4f normals even in Burnout); Counter-hit/Punish Counter puts the opponent into a limited juggle state that allows the 6HK follow-up to combo; 214MK combos from canceled 2MP/2HP/5HK (these cancels also frame trap on block); cannot perform follow-up attacks on whiff; lacks natural juggle potential but can juggle after DR~4HP (free juggle state) for a powerful 1-bar corner combo (DR~4HP > 214MK, 4HP > 236HK, 623MP); opponents can beat all follow-ups with invincible reversals (but standard 6f reversals will not punish 214MK); if the opponent attempts to punish 214MK, the 6LK follow-up will frame trap on block (must delay 6LK vs. Burnout)

Slow startup, only combos naturally from the first hit of 5HK (requires Drive Rush or Punish Counter to combo from 2HP, 4HP launch, or 5HK 2nd hit); 214HK cannot frame trap when canceled from a normal (except for Burnout + Drive Rush into 2MP/2HP/5HK); combos naturally into all follow-ups including 6HK; cancel into 6HK follow-up leaves a 7f gap on block (can frame trap 4f normals in Burnout); 2f extra recovery on Perfect Parry only; if the 1st hit is Perfect Parried, 2nd hit will interrupt any punish slower than 5f startup (trades with 6f attacks); cannot perform follow-up attacks if both hits whiff; carries Counter-hit/Punish Counter advantage through both hits; can juggle after DR~4HP (easier execution but less damaging than his MP Tiger Shot juggle sequence); opponents can beat all follow-ups with invincible reversals (but standard 6f reversals will not punish 214HK)

Similar to HK version but faster (can cancel from more starters like 2HP, 4HP launch, and 5HK 2nd hit); combos naturally into all follow-ups including 6HK; cancel into 6HK follow-up leaves a 7f gap on block (can frame trap 4f normals in Burnout); 2f extra recovery on Perfect Parry only; if the 1st hit is Perfect Parried, 2nd hit will interrupt any punish slower than 5f startup (trades with 6f attacks); cannot perform follow-up attacks if both hits whiff; carries Counter-hit/Punish Counter advantage through both hits; opponents can beat all follow-ups with invincible reversals (but standard 6f reversals will not punish 214KK)

Mixup tool that is unsafe on block; the threat of overhead makes ~6MK follow-up stronger while the threat of a frame trap makes ~6HK follow-up stronger; safe vs. Burnout but no longer frame traps (unless the 6LK input is delayed from 214LK/MK); puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (e.g. after Counter-hit 214LK/MK); causes immediate knockdown on Counter-hit/Punish Counter; loses to reversal Drive Impact after blocked 214LK/MK (but safe after 214HK unless the 6LK input is delayed); if used from a 2-light chain, opponent is in range for Throw or 2LK~5LP chain (too far if starting with 3-light chain)

Mixup tool that is safe on block; +1 vs. Burnout (but no longer frame traps and has no real looping pressure); the threat of overhead makes ~6MK follow-up stronger while the threat of a frame trap makes ~6HK follow-up stronger; puts opponents into limited juggle OTG bounce state on counter-hit or airborne hit (KD +47, can juggle into 623MP, SA2, SA3, 2HK, or 236LPMP which combos to SA1 in the corner); safe to reversal Drive Impact after blocked 214KK unless the 6LK input is delayed

Whiffs on crouching opponents; 2f extra recovery on whiff; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (only allows 623LP/PP juggle in the corner, or 623MP from CH/PC 214LK/MK launch); frame data vs. crouch from 214LK/214MK: -19 oH / -26 oB / KD +51 onPC launch; frame data vs. crouch from 214HK: -17 oH / -24 oB / -13 onPC (214HK keeps opponent crouching on Punish Counter); safe to reversal Drive Impact after blocked 214K; 5f blockstring gap after 214LK/MK (loses to reversal standing/crouching 4f normals); 3f blockstring gap after 214HK (frame trap vs. standing normals but still loses to reversal crouching normals); risky to attempt on block, but the threat of the overhead and frame trap from ~6LK follow-up can condition opponents to stand block or parry; opponent cannot walk back out of throw range on block

Whiffs on crouching opponents; 2f extra recovery on whiff; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (no midscreen juggle besides SA2/SA3 cancel); in the corner, can juggle into 623MP/PP, 2HK, or SA2 from a grounded hit, in addition to 236LK, 236LPMP, SA1, or SA3 on an airborne connect (e.g. 4HP launch or DI wallsplat); frame data vs. crouch from 214KK: -17 oH / -24 oB / -13 onPC; safe to reversal Drive Impact after blocked 214KK; 3f blockstring gap after 214KK (frame trap vs. standing normals but still loses to reversal crouching normals); risky to attempt on block, but the threat of the overhead and frame trap from ~6LK follow-up can condition opponents to stand block or parry; opponent cannot walk back out of throw range on block

Connects on both standing/crouching opponents; launches opponent into a limited juggle state; only combos naturally from 214HK (requires juggle state for LK/MK versions, like a CH/PC Tiger Nexus); after blocked 214LK/MK, interruptible 9f blockstring gap (5f gap vs. Burnout, loses to 4f normals); after blocked 214HK, interruptible 7f blockstring gap (frame trap vs. Burnout); unsafe to reversal Drive Impact and susceptible to Perfect Parry on reaction (becomes DI-safe from 214HK if opponent delays it by 2f or longer); opponent is left inside throw range on block (but Sagat cannot shimmy an immediate throw tech)

Connects on both standing/crouching opponents; launches opponent into a limited juggle state; combos naturally from 214KK; after blocked 214KK, interruptible 7f blockstring gap (frame trap vs. Burnout); unsafe to reversal Drive Impact and susceptible to Perfect Parry on reaction (becomes DI-safe from 214KK if opponent delays it by 2f or longer); opponent is left inside throw range on block (but Sagat cannot shimmy an immediate throw tech)

8-hit Super projectile; can be used while OD Tiger Shot is on-screen (but not meterless Tiger Shot); fast travel speed allows it to be used in long range juggles; projectile speed is not affected by button strength

Goes into one of 4 follow-ups after frame 76 on hit (depending on which direction is held while clutching the opponent); Sagat's best reversal Super (but is still slow enough to be baited by an opponent's safejab setup); can be used as a projectile counter from about half screen; Sagat has travel time throughout the active frames (takes longer than SA3 to reach full range)
Highest damage variant of SA2; leaves the opponent far away with no oki; has significant corner carry (over 1/2 screen)

Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state (juggle counter is always set to 2 regardless of previous juggle state); Hard Knockdown if the opponent hits the ground instead of being juggled; useful for corner carry, building back some Super gauge, and getting a good mix of damage + oki (but usually results in less damage than Tiger Raid)
Switches sides with opponent; leaves the opponent far away with no oki
Leaves the opponent close to Sagat for stronger oki than other versions; can walk up for a strike/throw/shimmy mixup; gives enough advantage for an immediate 6MP overhead

Cinematic time regenerates ~1.9 Drive bars for Sagat; only 2f startup when canceled from Tiger Uppercut; can be used as a projectile counter from about half screen; slow startup makes it a risky wakeup reversal option; total damage scaling from anti-air Tiger Uppercut is 20-40% depending on which strength was used (weaker strength gives higher scaling)

Available at 25% HP or below; cinematic time regenerates ~1.9 Drive bars for Sagat; only 2f startup when canceled from Tiger Uppercut; can be used as a projectile counter from about half screen; slow startup makes it a risky wakeup reversal option; total damage scaling from anti-air Tiger Uppercut is 20-40% depending on which strength was used (weaker strength gives higher scaling)

Frame Data Tables / Hitbox Explanation - SF6

Red: Attack hitbox
Pink: Throw hitbox
Green: Hurtbox (strikes/projectiles)

Certain move properties, like Projectile Invuln or Air Invuln, may be printed onto the hurtbox and listed in the move description

A complete lack of hurtboxes represents full invulnerability

Blue: Throw hurtbox

Throw will succeed if the pink throw hitbox overlaps with the blue throwable hurtbox

Opponent must be on the ground (except for Air Throws which only target airborne opponents)

Teal: Unique/Interaction box

Applies character-specific effects when two of these hitboxes overlap

Examples: Rashid's air current, Blanka's electric moves + Blanka-chan, Guile's Sonic Blade + Sonic Boom

Purple: Armor/Counter Hitbox

Can appear on top of green hurtboxes or replace them entirely

Orange: Projectile Clash hitbox

Not a projectile itself, but interacts with and destroys projectiles of the same priority

Light Orange box on Drive Impact : represents the "cinematic DI Slowdown" interaction hitboxes

How many frames a move remains active (can hurt opponents) for. For projectiles with a maximum active period, a value may be listed in [brackets], but this number is not factored into the move's total frame count.
For multi-hit moves with no gaps between the active hitboxes, active frames are listed as X,Y (or sometimes X*Y)

For multi-hit moves with gaps between hits, active frames are listed as X(n)Y where n = the frame gap between hitboxes.

Available options for canceling one move into another move.
"Chn": Chain cancel (Light normals; specific chain options listed in Description)

"TC": Target Combo

"Sp": Special move

"SA": Super Art (if a number is listed, refers only to that specific Super; SA3 = Lv.3 Super Art)

"Jmp": Jump cancel (usually on hit only, if applicable)

"SS": Serenity Stream (Chun-Li's stance)

"PS": Prowler Stance (Alex's stance)
If one hit of a multi-hit attack is cancelable, this can be indicated with (1st), (2nd), etc.

Occasionally, a move can be canceled only into a specific follow-up (e.g. Dee Jay [4]6P > 22PP); this can be indicated by listing the move input in the Cancel field, or with an asterisk that is explained in the move notes (Sp*)

Hitconfirm reaction windows into Special Moves, Target Combos, and Super Arts.
Refers to the amount of time (in frames) you have to cancel one attack into another attack on reaction
e.g. most cancelable 2MKs have a 13 frame window to cancel into a Special/Super on reaction, making them nearly impossible to hitconfirm

Counts from the first frame the attack connects until the final cancelable frame
Visual effects like hitsparks and HP drain do not actually occur until frame 2; the first frame is still counted to keep the numbers consistent with previous games, and because it is technically possible to start reacting to the character's reeling animation on frame 1

If a Target Combo is cancelable into another attack, the hitconfirm window will include the entire sequence starting from the first hit
If there is a frame gap on block between hits of the TC, the hitconfirm window may also be included for just the followup hit

Some sequences like Ken's 5MP~HP TC may have a range of values listed (43f~47f). In this example, inputting 5MP~HP at its usual timing gives a 43f hitconfirm into a Special/Super. Delaying the chain into HP gives more total time for the final hitconfirm.

Attack damage on hit. Multi-hit moves may have the damage listed for individual hits as X,Y (or sometimes X*Y). Sometimes a move's damage changes depending on which active frame connects, or on cinematic vs. non-cinematic hits; in this case, multiple values may be listed, and it will be clarified in the move description.

Some moves cause additional damage scaling in combos. Refer to Game Data page for a more detailed breakdown.
Scaling Types:

Starter: When a move begins the combo , the next attack is scaled by X percent
e.g. Ryu 2MK (20% Starter) > Hadoken: Hadoken is at 80% damage scaling

Combo: When a move is comboed into , the next attack is scaled by X percent or X number of hits
e.g. Ryu 2HP > OD High Blade Kick (2-Hit Combo Scaling) > Shoryuken: Shoryuken is at 70% damage scaling (100% > 100% > [skip 80%] > 70%)

e.g. Cammy 5HP > OD Spiral Arrow (5% Combo Scaling) > Cannon Spike: Cannon Spike is at 75% damage scaling (100% > 100% > [80-5 = 75%])

Immediate: When a move is comboed into , this attack is scaled by X percent
e.g. Drive Impact Crumple (20% Starter) > Throw (20% Immediate): Throw is at 60% damage scaling

Multiplier: A damage scaling multiplier applies after Perfect Parry (50%) and mid-combo Drive Rush (15%). Any hits in the combo continue their usual damage scaling, but reduced by these amounts. These can bring the minimum scaling below the usual 10%, and they stack with each other; as a result, the minimum scaling can reach 4% using a long Drive Rush combo after Perfect Parry.

Minimum Scaling: The lowest damage scaling that can be applied to an attack. Super Art Level 1/2/3 generally has 30%/40%/50% minimum scaling respectively. This ensures the attack will still do reasonable damage even at the end of a heavily scaled combo.

Refers to the frame advantage when canceling a normal, command normal, or Target Combo into Drive Rush on hit or block (abbreviated as DRC for Drive Rush Cancel). This is calculated at the moment a follow-up attack can be input, not at the moment the character can block or perform movement options. An attack that with DRC +8 on Hit can link into an 8-frame attack, and DRC +4 on Block can create a true blockstring into a 4-frame attack.
Note that any DRC on Block worse than +4 cannot form a true blockstring, allowing the opponent to interrupt with an invincible reversal. Most light normals are slightly negative after a DRC on block, meaning the opponent can mash their fastest normal to guarantee a counter-hit (though this requires fast reactions). The attacking character could punish this with Light > DRC into an immediate invincible attack, but this would be an incredibly expensive and high-risk gambit.

Most airborne command normals, special moves, and Super Arts put the user in a "Forced Knockdown" state. While in this state, an air knockdown will occur when being hit by any attack, even if it would otherwise cause an air reset.
As an example, Ryu's 2HP causes an air reset when used as an anti-air. Against a move like Cammy's Hooligan Combination, however, the 2HP puts her into an air knockdown state. This allows Ryu to successfully cancel 2HP into Shoryuken for a juggle, similar to how a Drive Impact wall splat works. Taking advantage of Forced Knockdown juggles is important for dealing with moves like Ken's Dragonlash, Dhalsim's Air Teleport, or Kimberly's 6HK~Hop sequence.

Moves that already cause an air knockdown, like most j.MP air-to-airs, will not display the "Forced Knockdown" message.

Refers to the direction an attack must be blocked. L is for Low attacks (must be blocked crouching), H is for High attacks/overheads (must be blocked standing), LH is for attacks that can be blocked crouching or standing. T is for Throw attacks which cannot be blocked.

When a character is put into an Air Knockdown state, it is often possible to follow up with a Juggle attack before they hit the ground. In the simplest terms, there are 2 main juggle states:
Free Juggle: any attack can juggle, causing an Air Reset or an Air Knockdown

Limited Juggle: only specific attacks with juggle potential may juggle

The following is a more detailed overview of the SF6 juggle system:

Juggle Count (JC) : The status of the character being juggled. A high JC limits which attacks can work in juggles.

JC0: free juggle state - any attack that can hit an airborne opponent will work

JC1+: limited juggle state - juggle only works if the attack's Juggle Limit ≥ defender's Juggle Count
A juggle count of -1 represents a crumple state; this can lead to a grounded or airborne hit depending on timing

Juggle Start (JS) : When starting a juggle, the opponent's JC will be set to this value. May be different vs. standing and airborne opponents.

Attack with Juggle Start value of 3 will put opponent at JC3, so only attacks with Juggle Limit value ≥ 3 can follow up

Even for attacks that don't normally start a juggle, this is relevant for Forced Knockdown and Crumple situations

Juggle Increase (JI) : When opponent is already in a juggle state, attacks will increase the opponent's JC by this amount.

Airborne opponent at JC1 followed by attack with Juggle Increase value of 3 will set opponent to JC4

Juggle Limit (JL) : Property of an attack hitbox that determines whether it connects on a juggled opponent. The JL must be ≥ the opponent's JC to hit successfully.

An uppercut with a JL value of 5 will connect on an opponent at JC5 or below, but will whiff on JC6 opponent

Most normals have a JL value of 0, meaning they only work in Free Juggle (JC0) states

Some multi-hit attacks have different JL values on each hit, so a 3-hit move may only hit twice in juggles

An example to tie everything together:

An attack (JS3) launches opponent into the air (Opponent now at JC3)

Followed up with an attack (JI2/JL4); it connects, because JL4 ≥ JC3 (Opponent now at JC5)

Attempts to juggle again with same attack (JL4), but whiffs because JL4 < JC5 (Opponent hits the ground)

Drive Rush notes:

DR normals have a Juggle Start/Increase value of 0

DR normals have +3 added to their usual Juggle Limit

More recently, the official definitions used by Capcom are slightly different than these community-designated terms. When reading official patch notes, the following terms are used instead:

Combo Count Initial Value

Combo Count Additional Value

Combo Count Upper Limit

These are frame advantage values when the attack hits or is blocked. If the number is positive, then the move will recover before the defender can act again. If the number is negative, the defender will be able to act before the attacker and maybe even punish. KD refers to knockdown on hit, and the listed KD Advantage refers to how many frames the attacker can act before the defender finishes their wakeup animation.
Note that generally, there is an extra +2 hit advantage on Counterhits and +4 hit advantage on Punish Counters (exceptions are noted in the description).

How many frames it takes for a move to finish after the active frames have finished. For projectiles, recovery is considered to begin after the first active frame.
Moves with different recovery values on hit/block/whiff may have multiple values listed like X(Y), with specific details listed in the description.

How many frames it takes before the move becomes 'active' or have a hit box. The last startup frame and the first active frame are the same frame, meaning all values are written as Startup + 1.
Moves with multiple relevant startup values may be listed as X(Y); for example, a move that hits airborne first before hitting grounded opponents, or a 2-hit move where the first hit whiffs at some ranges.

Some moves play out an extended recovery animation when no other button/direction is input (for crouching moves, it applies when holding any down direction). These are often referred to as "actionable recovery" frames; in some games, the term IASA (Interruptible As Soon As) refers to the frame that Actionable Recovery begins.
Letting the Actionable Recovery frames play out can change the character's position, potentially setting up spacing traps by recovering farther away. For example, Manon 5HP will recover much farther away from the opponent if no input is performed immediately after her recovery; holding back or down-back to block will keep her much closer to the opponent.

Introduction

edit

A young wrestler considered to be the next big thing. He debuted with his adoptive father Tom as his trainer, but was quickly made a heel due to his perceived surliness.

Debuting in Street Fighter III and returning from SFV, Alex is once again a grappler specializing in burst movement and relentless pressure . Where Manon's gameplan is about mixups, Lily’s about stock based plus frames, and Zangief's is about landing the SPD, Alex instead is a high-aggression, high mobility brawler who specializes at getting into medium-close range and forcing your opponent into constant guesses with relentless frame advantage, attacks that hold your Drive Gauge hostage, and big damage once he lands a clean hit.

Alex’s pressure on knockdown is some of the most suffocating offense to deal with in Street Fighter 6. He can approach above, behind, low, or the front, and each has a variety of options, attributes, and follow ups. Armored attacks that leave him plus, command grabs, and sneaky resets -- and that’s only scratching the surface.

Alex's buttons are long reaching and strong, giving him good pokes that allow him to roll into his game plan. 5MK has incredible range for harassing enemies, 5HK is excellent as a big punish and trap tool, and 5HP has an utterly gargantuan disjointed hitbox to win poke wars. Both of the standing heavies can be charged too, which gives him better frame data and unique properties (like the ability to special cancel from Charged 5HP ). 5MP and 2MP are his go-to cancelable pokes, and his 5LK can be linked after certain moves for longer combo extensions. His 5MP can be followed up with a new Target Combo called Palm Strikes , which creates a safe frame trap on block while setting up Prowler Stance oki if it knocks down.

Condition them to block with Flash Axe , his brand new light and medium variant of the powerful Flash Chop. Axe is safer on block and easier to combo into, as the powerful Chop only cancels properly on charged 5HP or 2HP . Aerial Knee Smash returns as his anti-air special; the light and medium versions are extremely fast and both give good oki, while the heavy is your ideal combo tool. Power Bomb and Power Drop are Alex's high-damage command throws, and it even retains the Street Fighter III 'back turn' mechanic, where moves that cause your opponent to spin before the throw (such as Heavy Lariat or Flash Chop) pay out better screen positioning and damage.

Brand new to Alex's kit is Prowler Stance , which functions like a more versatile version of Chun Li's Serenity Stream that can be performed in neutral or canceled from specific combo starters. He ducks low to the ground in a low-profile stance, and while he can't block or crouch under projectiles, he gains access to a vast arsenal of normal and special follow-ups. Alex gains a long-range chainable jab called Palm Thrust that cancels into specials or most other Prowler follow-ups. Air Stampede and Slash Elbow are terrific approach tools using both aerial or grounded movement, respectively. Tactical Hop allows Alex to juke OD reversals or sneak in a crafty cross-up at close range. Sweep Combination is a low Target Combo that gives good oki and big damage on Counter-hit . Shoulder Launcher can punish any aerial move on reaction, including jump-ins, safe specials like Sumo Headbutt or Blanka Ball, and even some airborne Supers that would otherwise punish Alex's stance. Heavy Lariat leads to combos on hit or pressure on block; by charging it up, it gains more block advantage and 2 hits of armor that can beat the opponent's Drive Impact , OD reversal, or other attempted counters. When Alex has them conditioned to only block or Parry, he can throw them with Hyper Takedown , which is functionally a normal throw that can be safe if the opponent tries to jump away. From farther away, the leaping command throw Dangerous Armbar can catch standing opponents or blow through any projectile in the game on reaction; it becomes the more devastating DDT if it lands as a Punish Counter , which will make opponents think twice about trying to parry any of Alex's approach options. The sheer variety of offensive weapons at his disposal makes any knockdown incredibly stressful for the opponent.

This incredible oki roulette comes at a cost; Alex's defensive tools are subpar, with no OD reversal and generally slow Supers that can be blocked in many oki setups. He has relatively few cancelable normals, and is notably lacking cancels from low pokes or from safe heavy pokes (except for the highly reactable Charged 5HP ), limiting his ability to control the midrange and punish back walks. Power Bomb deals solid damage, but the range drops off dramatically on faster versions, making it much easier to escape some pressure strings. While Prowler Stance is phenomenal, there are limited ways to cancel into it and his movement is limited to dashes, jumps, and attacks while in the stance. He also lacks a standard throw loop, forcing him to either use Hyper Takedown or spend meter on Drive Rush , while his wide hurtbox makes him more susceptible to throw loops himself.

All in all, if you like big damage, relentless offense, or you just really like looking at his muscles, Alex has a 141 ⅔ percent chance of being your character.

Avoid if you dislike:

STRETCH 'EM : Hard knockdowns and looping pressure in and out of Prowler Stance, letting Alex maintain a terrifying offense.

Applies character-specific effects when two of these hitboxes overlap

Examples: Rashid's air current, Blanka's electric moves + Blanka-chan, Guile's Sonic Blade + Sonic Boom

Purple: Armor/Counter Hitbox

Can appear on top of green hurtboxes or replace them entirely

Orange: Projectile Clash hitbox

Not a projectile itself, but interacts with and destroys projectiles of the same priority

Light Orange box on Drive Impact : represents the "cinematic DI Slowdown" interaction hitboxes

Active

How many frames a move remains active (can hurt opponents) for. For projectiles with a maximum active period, a value may be listed in [brackets], but this number is not factored into the move's total frame count.
For multi-hit moves with no gaps between the active hitboxes, active frames are listed as X,Y (or sometimes X*Y)

For multi-hit moves with gaps between hits, active frames are listed as X(n)Y where n = the frame gap between hitboxes.

Cancel

Available options for canceling one move into another move.
"Chn": Chain cancel (Light normals; specific chain options listed in Description)

"TC": Target Combo

"Sp": Special move

"SA": Super Art (if a number is listed, refers only to that specific Super; SA3 = Lv.3 Super Art)

"Jmp": Jump cancel (usually on hit only, if applicable)

"SS": Serenity Stream (Chun-Li's stance)

"PS": Prowler Stance (Alex's stance)
If one hit of a multi-hit attack is cancelable, this can be indicated with (1st), (2nd), etc.

Occasionally, a move can be canceled only into a specific follow-up (e.g. Dee Jay [4]6P > 22PP); this can be indicated by listing the move input in the Cancel field, or with an asterisk that is explained in the move notes (Sp*)

Cancel Hitconfirm Windows

Hitconfirm reaction windows into Special Moves, Target Combos, and Super Arts.
Refers to the amount of time (in frames) you have to cancel one attack into another attack on reaction
e.g. most cancelable 2MKs have a 13 frame window to cancel into a Special/Super on reaction, making them nearly impossible to hitconfirm

Counts from the first frame the attack connects until the final cancelable frame
Visual effects like hitsparks and HP drain do not actually occur until frame 2; the first frame is still counted to keep the numbers consistent with previous games, and because it is technically possible to start reacting to the character's reeling animation on frame 1

If a Target Combo is cancelable into another attack, the hitconfirm window will include the entire sequence starting from the first hit
If there is a frame gap on block between hits of the TC, the hitconfirm window may also be included for just the followup hit

Some sequences like Ken's 5MP~HP TC may have a range of values listed (43f~47f). In this example, inputting 5MP~HP at its usual timing gives a 43f hitconfirm into a Special/Super. Delaying the chain into HP gives more total time for the final hitconfirm.

Damage

Attack damage on hit. Multi-hit moves may have the damage listed for individual hits as X,Y (or sometimes X*Y). Sometimes a move's damage changes depending on which active frame connects, or on cinematic vs. non-cinematic hits; in this case, multiple values may be listed, and it will be clarified in the move description.

Damage Scaling

Some moves cause additional damage scaling in combos. Refer to Game Data page for a more detailed breakdown.
Scaling Types:

Starter: When a move begins the combo , the next attack is scaled by X percent
e.g. Ryu 2MK (20% Starter) > Hadoken: Hadoken is at 80% damage scaling

Combo: When a move is comboed into , the next attack is scaled by X percent or X number of hits
e.g. Ryu 2HP > OD High Blade Kick (2-Hit Combo Scaling) > Shoryuken: Shoryuken is at 70% damage scaling (100% > 100% > [skip 80%] > 70%)

e.g. Cammy 5HP > OD Spiral Arrow (5% Combo Scaling) > Cannon Spike: Cannon Spike is at 75% damage scaling (100% > 100% > [80-5 = 75%])

Immediate: When a move is comboed into , this attack is scaled by X percent
e.g. Drive Impact Crumple (20% Starter) > Throw (20% Immediate): Throw is at 60% damage scaling

Multiplier: A damage scaling multiplier applies after Perfect Parry (50%) and mid-combo Drive Rush (15%). Any hits in the combo continue their usual damage scaling, but reduced by these amounts. These can bring the minimum scaling below the usual 10%, and they stack with each other; as a result, the minimum scaling can reach 4% using a long Drive Rush combo after Perfect Parry.

Minimum Scaling: The lowest damage scaling that can be applied to an attack. Super Art Level 1/2/3 generally has 30%/40%/50% minimum scaling respectively. This ensures the attack will still do reasonable damage even at the end of a heavily scaled combo.

Drive Rush Cancel Advantage

Refers to the frame advantage when canceling a normal, command normal, or Target Combo into Drive Rush on hit or block (abbreviated as DRC for Drive Rush Cancel). This is calculated at the moment a follow-up attack can be input, not at the moment the character can block or perform movement options. An attack that with DRC +8 on Hit can link into an 8-frame attack, and DRC +4 on Block can create a true blockstring into a 4-frame attack.
Note that any DRC on Block worse than +4 cannot form a true blockstring, allowing the opponent to interrupt with an invincible reversal. Most light normals are slightly negative after a DRC on block, meaning the opponent can mash their fastest normal to guarantee a counter-hit (though this requires fast reactions). The attacking character could punish this with Light > DRC into an immediate invincible attack, but this would be an incredibly expensive and high-risk gambit.

Forced Knockdown

Most airborne command normals, special moves, and Super Arts put the user in a "Forced Knockdown" state. While in this state, an air knockdown will occur when being hit by any attack, even if it would otherwise cause an air reset.
As an example, Ryu's 2HP causes an air reset when used as an anti-air. Against a move like Cammy's Hooligan Combination, however, the 2HP puts her into an air knockdown state. This allows Ryu to successfully cancel 2HP into Shoryuken for a juggle, similar to how a Drive Impact wall splat works. Taking advantage of Forced Knockdown juggles is important for dealing with moves like Ken's Dragonlash, Dhalsim's Air Teleport, or Kimberly's 6HK~Hop sequence.

Moves that already cause an air knockdown, like most j.MP air-to-airs, will not display the "Forced Knockdown" message.

Guard

Refers to the direction an attack must be blocked. L is for Low attacks (must be blocked crouching), H is for High attacks/overheads (must be blocked standing), LH is for attacks that can be blocked crouching or standing. T is for Throw attacks which cannot be blocked.

Juggles

When a character is put into an Air Knockdown state, it is often possible to follow up with a Juggle attack before they hit the ground. In the simplest terms, there are 2 main juggle states:
Free Juggle: any attack can juggle, causing an Air Reset or an Air Knockdown

Limited Juggle: only specific attacks with juggle potential may juggle

The following is a more detailed overview of the SF6 juggle system:

Juggle Count (JC) : The status of the character being juggled. A high JC limits which attacks can work in juggles.

JC0: free juggle state - any attack that can hit an airborne opponent will work

JC1+: limited juggle state - juggle only works if the attack's Juggle Limit ≥ defender's Juggle Count
A juggle count of -1 represents a crumple state; this can lead to a grounded or airborne hit depending on timing

Juggle Start (JS) : When starting a juggle, the opponent's JC will be set to this value. May be different vs. standing and airborne opponents.

Attack with Juggle Start value of 3 will put opponent at JC3, so only attacks with Juggle Limit value ≥ 3 can follow up

Even for attacks that don't normally start a juggle, this is relevant for Forced Knockdown and Crumple situations

Juggle Increase (JI) : When opponent is already in a juggle state, attacks will increase the opponent's JC by this amount.

Airborne opponent at JC1 followed by attack with Juggle Increase value of 3 will set opponent to JC4

Juggle Limit (JL) : Property of an attack hitbox that determines whether it connects on a juggled opponent. The JL must be ≥ the opponent's JC to hit successfully.

An uppercut with a JL value of 5 will connect on an opponent at JC5 or below, but will whiff on JC6 opponent

Most normals have a JL value of 0, meaning they only work in Free Juggle (JC0) states

Some multi-hit attacks have different JL values on each hit, so a 3-hit move may only hit twice in juggles

An example to tie everything together:

An attack (JS3) launches opponent into the air (Opponent now at JC3)

Followed up with an attack (JI2/JL4); it connects, because JL4 ≥ JC3 (Opponent now at JC5)

Attempts to juggle again with same attack (JL4), but whiffs because JL4 < JC5 (Opponent hits the ground)

Drive Rush notes:

DR normals have a Juggle Start/Increase value of 0

DR normals have +3 added to their usual Juggle Limit

More recently, the official definitions used by Capcom are slightly different than these community-designated terms. When reading official patch notes, the following terms are used instead:

Combo Count Initial Value

Combo Count Additional Value

Combo Count Upper Limit

On Hit/Block

These are frame advantage values when the attack hits or is blocked. If the number is positive, then the move will recover before the defender can act again. If the number is negative, the defender will be able to act before the attacker and maybe even punish. KD refers to knockdown on hit, and the listed KD Advantage refers to how many frames the attacker can act before the defender finishes their wakeup animation.
Note that generally, there is an extra +2 hit advantage on Counterhits and +4 hit advantage on Punish Counters (exceptions are noted in the description).

Recovery

How many frames it takes for a move to finish after the active frames have finished. For projectiles, recovery is considered to begin after the first active frame.
Moves with different recovery values on hit/block/whiff may have multiple values listed like X(Y), with specific details listed in the description.

Startup

How many frames it takes before the move becomes 'active' or have a hit box. The last startup frame and the first active frame are the same frame, meaning all values are written as Startup + 1.
Moves with multiple relevant startup values may be listed as X(Y); for example, a move that hits airborne first before hitting grounded opponents, or a 2-hit move where the first hit whiffs at some ranges.

IASA / Actionable Recovery

Some moves play out an extended recovery animation when no other button/direction is input (for crouching moves, it applies when holding any down direction). These are often referred to as "actionable recovery" frames; in some games, the term IASA (Interruptible As Soon As) refers to the frame that Actionable Recovery begins.
Letting the Actionable Recovery frames play out can change the character's position, potentially setting up spacing traps by recovering farther away. For example, Manon 5HP will recover much farther away from the opponent if no input is performed immediately after her recovery; holding back or down-back to block will keep her much closer to the opponent.

This attack with no charge is a standard punish counter normal like Terry’s Stand HK, so it gives a crumple on hit if hit on a Punish Counter or better which guarantees a Crouch MP from anywhere on the screen into a Flash Axe but on regular hit, it’s just a high damage poke with mediocre frame data. The move’s great for Punish Countering as it gives a launch up instead of a stagger on Punish Counter or better which is what leads into Alex’s more damaging combo routes (some of which are entirely meterless and deal as much damage as some character’s metered combos) so if there’s a button you know you’ll Punish Counter or a whiffed reversal that gives enough time to charge this attack, use this as your Punish starter since it’ll always give good damage even in burnout

Fast and long range jab that maintains the stance's Low Profile and crouching state; cancelable into other Prowler Stance moves (except Stance Exit, Forward/Back Dash, Hyper Takedown, or Slashing Elbow) and into standard specials / DI / DR; Alex remains in stance if not canceled (forced to exit after Perfect Parry); chained jabs form a true blockstring (can chain 4 jabs on hit or 3 on block); frame advantage compares the end of the jab recovery to the opponent's hitstun/blockstun but is only really relevant for tick throws with Hyper Takedown or when using Slashing Elbow afterward; can only tick throw into Hyper Takedown (Stance LP+LK) after 1 jab

Counter-hit/Punish Counter transitions into Falling Moon for higher damage, Hard Knockdown, and improved meter properties (regardless of whether 1st or 2nd hit connects); () refers to Falling Moon damage; not airborne despite the animation; puts opponents into a limited juggle state on normal hit; maintains Low Profile on frames 1-7 and considered crouching on frames 1-13; cannot hit cross-up but will autocorrect if input while dashing under the opponent (allows for side swap juggle routes); can be canceled into from Palm Jab

Can be held to gain damage, 2f extra blockstun, and armor properties; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Counter-hit (+8) / Punish Counter (+10) puts grounded opponents into a Backturned state that can link to 4MK or MP/OD Power Drop (can whiff at long range); shorter range vs. crouching opponents; great pressure tool for depleting the opponent's Drive gauge; can be canceled into from Palm Jab (up to 3 jabs vs. standing or 2 jabs vs. crouching); uncharged version comes out if button is held up to 12 frames; can be spaced out to hit on later active frames for better advantage (up to +8/+5); holding the button 1-5f results in 12f startup; holding the button 6-12f increases the total startup incrementally (up to a maximum startup of 20f); maintains Low Profile on frames 1-6 and crouch state on frames 1-14 (standing-sized hurtbox on frames 11-14)

More damage and blockstun than uncharged version; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Counter-hit (+8) / Punish Counter (+10) puts grounded opponents into a Backturned state that can link to 4MK or MP/OD Power Drop (can whiff at long range); armor absorbs 2 hits as long as the button continues to be held (armor lasts until the end of active frames); shorter range vs. crouching opponents; great pressure tool for depleting the opponent's Drive gauge; can be canceled into from Palm Jab but only combos on Punish Counter; can be spaced out to hit on later active frames for better advantage (up to +8/+7); button must be held 13f (early release ends the armor and results in uncharged version); maintains Low Profile on frames 1-16 and crouch state on frames 1-23 (standing-sized hurtbox on frames 20-23)

Distance: 1.157; much shorter trajectory and lower height than a standard jump; can perform air normals or Flying Cross Chop on frames 22-32 (buffers from frame 8~, then buffers a grounded normal if pressed on frame 33~); immediately loses low profile state and exits stance upon activation; prejump frames 1-2 are in a crouching state followed by a standing state on frames 3-6; Lower Body Projectile Invuln on frames 6-8 (helps jump over projectiles on startup); has a smaller body hurtbox on frames 6-33; 3f landing recovery like a regular jump but cannot block when landing from an empty jump; Alex is in a Counter-hit state for entire move duration; can be canceled into from Palm Jab

Can be steered left/right; cannot hit cross-up; Alex is considered grounded on the 2nd active frame (anti-air invuln specials will lose if they don't hit before this frame); Punish Counter puts opponents into a limited juggle OTG bounce state (Hard Knockdown if no move is juggled afterward); immediately loses low profile state and exits stance upon activation (remains crouching on frames 1-8 with a standing-sized hurtbox on frames 5-8); very short hitstop gives little time for opponent to make a decision on block (significantly longer hitstop on Punish Counter for easier juggle confirms); stomp is block reactable but difficult to anti-air (can hold back to cause many anti-airs to whiff at some ranges); can intentionally whiff over the opponent to bait parry (opponent can option select with 4~4MPMK to option select a parry + Drive Rush, though the timing is strict to punish Alex); can be canceled into from Palm Jab

Hitconfirmable (but unsafe) long range sweep; Counter-hit/Punish Counter transitions into Flying Suplex for extra damage, meter, and a Hard Knockdown (no difference between 1st or 2nd hit of the TC when this happens); puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (allows TC follow-up to combo); Alex remains in stance after recovery except on Perfect Parry or when Flying Suplex connects; maintains Low Profile and crouch state for entire duration; 3f blockstring gap between hits (will frame trap if opponent attempts a punish too early); can be canceled into from Palm Jab (consistent combo ender at any range)

Counter-hit/Punish Counter transitions into Flying Suplex for extra damage, meter, and a Hard Knockdown (no difference between 1st or 2nd hit of the TC when this happens); Alex remains in stance after recovery except on Perfect Parry or when Flying Suplex connects; maintains Low Profile and crouch state for entire duration; 3f blockstring gap between hits (will frame trap if opponent attempts a punish too early); leaves Alex +1 after manual Stance Exit for corner oki; can whiff when the first sweep connects at max range

Acts like a normal throw with extra range (can be teched); turns into Death Valley Bomb on Punish Counter (different animation with separate KD advantage and higher damage/meter properties); leads to good oki anywhere on screen; immediately loses low profile state and exits stance upon activation but retains crouching state on frames 1-7 with standing-sized hurtboxes; cannot be canceled into from Palm Jab (only in throw range after 1 jab on hit or block); a successful Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender; Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

Turns into Spiral DDT on Punish Counter (different animation with separate KD advantage and higher damage/meter properties); can only hit standing opponents; regular version gets strong meterless corner oki or Drive Rush midscreen oki; Punish Counter version can walk for meterless oki anywhere on screen; immediately loses low profile state and exits stance upon activation but retains crouching state on frames 1-14 (standing-sized hurtboxes on frames 9-14); can be canceled into from Palm Jab for a more effective tick throw; strong reaction counter to projectiles when already in stance (including invincible projectile Supers)

No true throw loop without Drive Rush (can dash + LP Power Bomb, dash up into spaced normals, or use Drive Rush for better strike/throw oki); DR~5HK leaves Alex +7/+2 anywhere on screen and in range for a tick command grab (HP in corner, OD midscreen); midscreen, can also hold the DR~5[HK] to throw off Perfect Parry timing or punish delay tech; a successful Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender; Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

Side switch; no real strike/throw oki in the corner but can pressure with Drive Rush normals; a successful Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender; Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

Leaves Alex at neutral advantage after forward dash for a pseudo-throw loop; Drive Rush allows real corner throw loops but gives weak midscreen oki; a successful Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender; Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously
See Drive Impact . Airborne connect gives spinning juggle state on Punish Counter or corner Wall Splat with variable height.

Performed by inputting 6HPHK during blockstun; 5f extra recovery on hit; freezes the screen for 4f during startup; 4f less hitstop on block compared to most Drive Reversals (changes the punish timing); see Drive Reversal .

Performed by holding 6HPHK on wakeup; 5f extra recovery on hit; does not have any screen freeze except for a 12f freeze when interacting with the opponent's throw hitbox (this also refunds 1 Drive bar after punishing the throw); 4f less hitstop on block compared to most Drive Reversals (changes the punish timing); see Drive Reversal .

See Drive Parry . Perfect Parrying has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack. Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 11 frames of recovery. After a Perfect Parry, all Super Gauge gain is reduced by 20% and Drive Gauge gain/damage is reduced by 50% for the entire punish combo.

See Drive Rush ; 1-bar version performed out of a Parry; startup refers to minimum time before an attack can cancel the Drive Rush animation (if performed immediately after a successful Parry, only 1+8 startup); the first 15 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack; the final 22 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack or movement option or blocking (except Parry); only Normal and Command Normal attacks are enhanced with +4 frame advantage and improved juggle properties; Distance: 0.393 (min/throw), 1.722 (min/block), 3.530 (max/final DR frame)

MPMK or 66 DP or 66

Drive Rush Cancel

See Drive Rush ; 3-bar version performed on hit/block from a cancelable normal; can also be performed on whiff from cancelable light normals; startup refers to minimum time before an attack can cancel the Drive Rush animation; the first 15 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack; the final 22 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack or movement option or blocking (except Parry); only Normal and Command Normal attacks are enhanced with +4 frame advantage and improved juggle properties

Safe on block if spaced from a light string and maintains pressure up close on hit; has both a strike hitbox and a separate 1-hit projectile clash box during the active frames; this allows Alex to hit the opponent even when clashing with higher-priority projectiles like Supers (though it doesn't dissipate any hits of the higher priority projectiles)

Can transition into Prowler Stance on hit; important combo tool that is relatively safe if spaced out; extends a large vertical combo-only hitbox for juggle consistency; has both a strike hitbox as well as a separate 1-hit projectile clash box on frames 16-20 (starting 1f before active); this allows Alex to hit the opponent even when clashing with higher-priority projectiles like Supers (though it doesn't dissipate any hits of the higher priority projectiles); can get midscreen oki with Drive Rush into a delayed button or throw; Prowler Stance cancel: KD +46 oH (variable on airborne opponents)

Puts opponent into Backturned state and Forces Stand on hit; slow startup but plus on block (leaves the opponent inside OD Power Bomb range for a tick throw); true blockstring from 5[HP] dealing significant Drive damage; has both a strike hitbox as well as a separate 1-hit projectile clash box on frames 25-29 (starting 1f before active); this allows Alex to hit the opponent even when clashing with higher-priority projectiles like Supers (though it doesn't dissipate any hits of the higher priority projectiles); recovery is cancelable on hit into Power Drop (63214P) or Collapsing Driver (4MK) on frame 40 (opponent must be grounded for these to connect); can omit the follow-up cancel and link normals afterward (lights on regular hit, 5MP on counter-hit, 2HP on Punish Counter)

2 hits; 1st hit keeps opponent grounded (SA2 cancel allows cinematic hit); 2nd hit puts opponents into a limited juggle state (SA2 cancel causes wall splat); can transition into Prowler Stance on hit; completely safe on block due to pushback; has both a strike hitbox as well as a separate 2-hit OD projectile clash box on frames 14-19 (starting 1f before active); this allows Alex to hit the opponent even when clashing with higher-priority projectiles like Supers (though it doesn't dissipate any hits of the higher priority projectiles); leads to good midscreen oki with Drive Rush or a 6-frame safe jump with j.HK (can often outspace 5f reversals as well); Prowler Stance cancel: KD +37 oH (variable on airborne opponents)

Anti-air grab (cannot hit grounded opponents); cannot hit cross-up; best overall anti-air at closer ranges due to its fast speed and upward trajectory; allows strong meterless oki in the corner or Drive Rush oki midscreen

Anti-air grab (cannot hit grounded opponents); cannot hit cross-up; more horizontal range and an extended combo-only hitbox make it useful in juggles; allows strong meterless oki in the corner or Drive Rush oki midscreen

Active frames 1-2 can hit grounded or airborne; active frames 3-8 can only hit airborne; Drive/Super meter gain only applies to the first hit when blocked; cannot hit cross-up; slow for anti-air purposes but the range can be used to punish landing recovery of divekicks or similar moves; useful as a combo ender even from max range light normals; allows strong meterless oki in the corner or Drive Rush oki midscreen

623KK 623XX or A[6S] or A[2S]

OD Aerial Knee Smash

Active frames 1-2 can hit grounded or airborne; active frames 3-8 can only hit airborne; Super meter gain only applies to the first hit when blocked; cannot hit cross-up; Hard Knockdown allows strong meterless oki anywhere on screen; combos and anti-airs in all the same situations as HK version (and even more lenient in juggles due to the faster startup)
Longest range / slowest startup version; useful in some oki situations (e.g. corner throw + dash) but less useful in tick throw scenarios; turns into Power Drop on backturned opponent
Medium range / startup version; turns into Power Drop on backturned opponent; can be used in some tick throw situations especially out of Drive Rush normals

Shortest range / fastest startup version; turns into Power Drop on backturned opponent; most useful for tick throws when the range allows it (like after 4MK on block at point blank); Alex's strongest meterless Drive Reversal punish (but can whiff when blocked at max range)

Startup of HP version with range in between LP/MP versions; most useful overall in tick throw scenarios; turns into Power Drop on backturned opponent; more consistent and slightly more damaging as a Drive Reversal punish than HP version

Switches sides with no real oki; no difference between strengths once the grab connects; the version that comes out after 236HP has more range than any standard version of Power Bomb (but can whiff at absolute max range vs. crouching opponents); () refers to Punish Counter damage, scaled damage refers to version canceled from 236HP combo starter; backturn connect can occur even without 236HP starter (e.g. after opponent jumps over Alex)

63214PP Backturn 63214XX or A[4S] Backturn

OD Power Drop

Switches sides and leads to Drive Rush oki even midscreen; cancelable into Omega Wing Buster by inputting PP (cannot hold buttons for the entire animation, input during the 2nd body slam); () refers to Punish Counter damage, scaled damage refers to version canceled from 236HP combo starter; the version that comes out after 236HP has more range than any standard version of Power Bomb (but can whiff at absolute max range vs. crouching opponents); the starter scaling affects Omega Wing Buster damage when punishing with a raw OD Power Drop, while the combo scaling affects it when canceled from HP Flash Chop; backturn connect can occur even without 236HP starter (e.g. after opponent jumps over Alex)

Does not switch sides; sets up a safe jump or Drive Rush oki anywhere on the screen; cannot be canceled into Omega Wing Buster; () refers to Punish Counter damage, scaled damage refers to version canceled from 236HP combo starter; maintains the same damage scaling as the preceding OD Power Drop (does not count as a separate move for scaling); backturn connect can occur even without 236HP starter (e.g. after opponent jumps over Alex)

Alex's best reversal option; sends opponent far away (oki only possible near the corner); puts opponent into a limited juggle state that can lead to trade combos depending on distance and the opponent's attack hitstun (e.g. fireball trade, early anti-air timing)

Causes a cinematic on grounded opponents and a wallsplat on airborne opponents (can juggle in the corner); wallsplat is a free juggle state if SA2 starts the combo (otherwise, maintains the existing juggle state); can choose which version to cancel into from OD Flash Chop (1st hit stays grounded, 2nd hit launches); effective fireball counter due to range and invincibility; cinematic version gives decent Drive Rush oki (but DR~Throw can only beat reversal 4f normals on wide characters like Alex, Marisa, Sagat, Blanka, E. Honda, and Zangief)

Can only be performed after OD Power Drop on a backturned opponent; 2800 damage refers to base damage without scaling (1680 is the most it can theoretically do at 60% scaling); fully invincible for the entire cinematic; pushes opponent a full screen away (no possible oki); PP input must be pressed rather than held for the entire throw cinematic (timing is around the 2nd body slam)

Cinematic time regenerates ~2 Drive bars for Alex; significantly less range than Alex's other Supers; poor oki after the cinematic (e.g. spaced DR~5MP or DR~2MK); has 2 different cinematics depending on whether it KOs the opponent

Available at 25% HP or below; cinematic time regenerates ~2.1 Drive bars for Alex; significantly less range than Alex's other Supers; better oki than standard SA3 (e.g. DR~Throw or DR~5HP into tick MP Power Bomb); has 2 different cinematics depending on whether it KOs the opponent

overview.title: Street Fighter 6/Ingrid
tables:
Spacial Oddities: An array of projectiles that can be used concurrently, an anti-air with a uniquely easy input, and a full-screen beam all come together to make for a tricky zoning game.

Cataclysmic Cutie: Having HUGE burst damage when loaded up on system and character resources.

Limbs of the Forbidden One: Strong pokes and whiff punishes that lead into Target Combos and further damage.

Hey! No Fair!: Being susceptible to virtually any kind of anti-fireball tool in midrange scenarios, due to the frame data/"stop-start" nature of her Sun Shot fireball. Spin Knuckles, Shoto Tatsus, Slides– if it has a whiff of projectile-invuln, and your opponent has a pulse, they can react, and it will punish. Risk awareness is advised.

God Complex: Managing a stock system to gain access to her full potential, and having to choose between Sun Crests and okizeme.

Depressurisation: Generally having a harder time sticking close enough after buttons pressure, as well as lacking in natural plus frames to better enforce any kind of respect.

Sun Shot ( 5S / 5[S] / 4S )
Cannot use the held version of horizontal fireballs, as this becomes the M version

A[ L ~ L ~ L ]: 5LP ~ 5LK ~ M Sun Rise
On Block: stops after 5LK

Auto-hitconfirm if opponent is hit by the 2nd light in the string

2L ~A[ 2L ~ L ~ L ]: 2LK ~ 2LK ~ 2LP ~ M Sun Rise
Variant ender that lets Ingrid get a Light Assist Combo from a chained starter

A[ M ~ M ~ M ~ M ]: 2MP ~ OD Sun Rise ~ SA2 ~ M Sun Rise
Burnout: 2MP ~ M Sun Rise

On Block: stops after OD Sun Rise (can manually input SA2 cancel)

A[ H ~ H ~ H ~ H ]: 5MP ~ MK ~ OD Sun Flare ~ SA3
No SA3 : ends with Forward Vanishing Sun (6KKK) instead

Burnout: 5MP ~ MK ~ H Sun Flare ~ SA3

Burnout + No SA3 : 1 Stock ends with L Sun Flare , 2 Stock ends with Forward Vanishing Sun (6KKK)

On Block: stops after 5MP ~ MK

2L is 2LK but switches to 2LP if chained into
2LP is unavailable outside of chains

5LP can be chained into from 2LK ( 2L ), but not when using the (A[ L ]) input
Ingrid can still get a 3-light confirm using manual inputs, or by starting with a manually linked A[ L ] ~ A[ L ] (delayed to avoid activating the Assist Combo)
Frame Data Tables / Hitbox Explanation - SF6

Red: Attack hitbox
Pink: Throw hitbox
Green: Hurtbox (strikes/projectiles)

Certain move properties, like Projectile Invuln or Air Invuln, may be printed onto the hurtbox and listed in the move description

A complete lack of hurtboxes represents full invulnerability

Blue: Throw hurtbox

Throw will succeed if the pink throw hitbox overlaps with the blue throwable hurtbox

Opponent must be on the ground (except for Air Throws which only target airborne opponents)

Teal: Unique/Interaction box

Applies character-specific effects when two of these hitboxes overlap

Examples: Rashid's air current, Blanka's electric moves + Blanka-chan, Guile's Sonic Blade + Sonic Boom

Purple: Armor/Counter Hitbox

Can appear on top of green hurtboxes or replace them entirely

Orange: Projectile Clash hitbox

Not a projectile itself, but interacts with and destroys projectiles of the same priority

Light Orange box on Drive Impact : represents the "cinematic DI Slowdown" interaction hitboxes

How many frames a move remains active (can hurt opponents) for. For projectiles with a maximum active period, a value may be listed in [brackets], but this number is not factored into the move's total frame count.
For multi-hit moves with no gaps between the active hitboxes, active frames are listed as X,Y (or sometimes X*Y)

For multi-hit moves with gaps between hits, active frames are listed as X(n)Y where n = the frame gap between hitboxes.

Available options for canceling one move into another move.
"Chn": Chain cancel (Light normals; specific chain options listed in Description)

"TC": Target Combo

"Sp": Special move

"SA": Super Art (if a number is listed, refers only to that specific Super; SA3 = Lv.3 Super Art)

"Jmp": Jump cancel (usually on hit only, if applicable)

"SS": Serenity Stream (Chun-Li's stance)

"PS": Prowler Stance (Alex's stance)
If one hit of a multi-hit attack is cancelable, this can be indicated with (1st), (2nd), etc.

Occasionally, a move can be canceled only into a specific follow-up (e.g. Dee Jay [4]6P > 22PP); this can be indicated by listing the move input in the Cancel field, or with an asterisk that is explained in the move notes (Sp*)

Hitconfirm reaction windows into Special Moves, Target Combos, and Super Arts.
Refers to the amount of time (in frames) you have to cancel one attack into another attack on reaction
e.g. most cancelable 2MKs have a 13 frame window to cancel into a Special/Super on reaction, making them nearly impossible to hitconfirm

Counts from the first frame the attack connects until the final cancelable frame
Visual effects like hitsparks and HP drain do not actually occur until frame 2; the first frame is still counted to keep the numbers consistent with previous games, and because it is technically possible to start reacting to the character's reeling animation on frame 1

If a Target Combo is cancelable into another attack, the hitconfirm window will include the entire sequence starting from the first hit
If there is a frame gap on block between hits of the TC, the hitconfirm window may also be included for just the followup hit

Some sequences like Ken's 5MP~HP TC may have a range of values listed (43f~47f). In this example, inputting 5MP~HP at its usual timing gives a 43f hitconfirm into a Special/Super. Delaying the chain into HP gives more total time for the final hitconfirm.

Attack damage on hit. Multi-hit moves may have the damage listed for individual hits as X,Y (or sometimes X*Y). Sometimes a move's damage changes depending on which active frame connects, or on cinematic vs. non-cinematic hits; in this case, multiple values may be listed, and it will be clarified in the move description.

Some moves cause additional damage scaling in combos. Refer to Game Data page for a more detailed breakdown.
Scaling Types:

Starter: When a move begins the combo , the next attack is scaled by X percent
e.g. Ryu 2MK (20% Starter) > Hadoken: Hadoken is at 80% damage scaling

Combo: When a move is comboed into , the next attack is scaled by X percent or X number of hits
e.g. Ryu 2HP > OD High Blade Kick (2-Hit Combo Scaling) > Shoryuken: Shoryuken is at 70% damage scaling (100% > 100% > [skip 80%] > 70%)

e.g. Cammy 5HP > OD Spiral Arrow (5% Combo Scaling) > Cannon Spike: Cannon Spike is at 75% damage scaling (100% > 100% > [80-5 = 75%])

Immediate: When a move is comboed into , this attack is scaled by X percent
e.g. Drive Impact Crumple (20% Starter) > Throw (20% Immediate): Throw is at 60% damage scaling

Multiplier: A damage scaling multiplier applies after Perfect Parry (50%) and mid-combo Drive Rush (15%). Any hits in the combo continue their usual damage scaling, but reduced by these amounts. These can bring the minimum scaling below the usual 10%, and they stack with each other; as a result, the minimum scaling can reach 4% using a long Drive Rush combo after Perfect Parry.

Minimum Scaling: The lowest damage scaling that can be applied to an attack. Super Art Level 1/2/3 generally has 30%/40%/50% minimum scaling respectively. This ensures the attack will still do reasonable damage even at the end of a heavily scaled combo.

Refers to the frame advantage when canceling a normal, command normal, or Target Combo into Drive Rush on hit or block (abbreviated as DRC for Drive Rush Cancel). This is calculated at the moment a follow-up attack can be input, not at the moment the character can block or perform movement options. An attack that with DRC +8 on Hit can link into an 8-frame attack, and DRC +4 on Block can create a true blockstring into a 4-frame attack.
Note that any DRC on Block worse than +4 cannot form a true blockstring, allowing the opponent to interrupt with an invincible reversal. Most light normals are slightly negative after a DRC on block, meaning the opponent can mash their fastest normal to guarantee a counter-hit (though this requires fast reactions). The attacking character could punish this with Light > DRC into an immediate invincible attack, but this would be an incredibly expensive and high-risk gambit.

Most airborne command normals, special moves, and Super Arts put the user in a "Forced Knockdown" state. While in this state, an air knockdown will occur when being hit by any attack, even if it would otherwise cause an air reset.
As an example, Ryu's 2HP causes an air reset when used as an anti-air. Against a move like Cammy's Hooligan Combination, however, the 2HP puts her into an air knockdown state. This allows Ryu to successfully cancel 2HP into Shoryuken for a juggle, similar to how a Drive Impact wall splat works. Taking advantage of Forced Knockdown juggles is important for dealing with moves like Ken's Dragonlash, Dhalsim's Air Teleport, or Kimberly's 6HK~Hop sequence.

Moves that already cause an air knockdown, like most j.MP air-to-airs, will not display the "Forced Knockdown" message.

Refers to the direction an attack must be blocked. L is for Low attacks (must be blocked crouching), H is for High attacks/overheads (must be blocked standing), LH is for attacks that can be blocked crouching or standing. T is for Throw attacks which cannot be blocked.

When a character is put into an Air Knockdown state, it is often possible to follow up with a Juggle attack before they hit the ground. In the simplest terms, there are 2 main juggle states:
Free Juggle: any attack can juggle, causing an Air Reset or an Air Knockdown

Limited Juggle: only specific attacks with juggle potential may juggle

The following is a more detailed overview of the SF6 juggle system:

Juggle Count (JC) : The status of the character being juggled. A high JC limits which attacks can work in juggles.

JC0: free juggle state - any attack that can hit an airborne opponent will work

JC1+: limited juggle state - juggle only works if the attack's Juggle Limit ≥ defender's Juggle Count
A juggle count of -1 represents a crumple state; this can lead to a grounded or airborne hit depending on timing

Juggle Start (JS) : When starting a juggle, the opponent's JC will be set to this value. May be different vs. standing and airborne opponents.

Attack with Juggle Start value of 3 will put opponent at JC3, so only attacks with Juggle Limit value ≥ 3 can follow up

Even for attacks that don't normally start a juggle, this is relevant for Forced Knockdown and Crumple situations

Juggle Increase (JI) : When opponent is already in a juggle state, attacks will increase the opponent's JC by this amount.

Airborne opponent at JC1 followed by attack with Juggle Increase value of 3 will set opponent to JC4

Juggle Limit (JL) : Property of an attack hitbox that determines whether it connects on a juggled opponent. The JL must be ≥ the opponent's JC to hit successfully.

An uppercut with a JL value of 5 will connect on an opponent at JC5 or below, but will whiff on JC6 opponent

Most normals have a JL value of 0, meaning they only work in Free Juggle (JC0) states

Some multi-hit attacks have different JL values on each hit, so a 3-hit move may only hit twice in juggles

An example to tie everything together:

An attack (JS3) launches opponent into the air (Opponent now at JC3)

Followed up with an attack (JI2/JL4); it connects, because JL4 ≥ JC3 (Opponent now at JC5)

Attempts to juggle again with same attack (JL4), but whiffs because JL4 < JC5 (Opponent hits the ground)

Drive Rush notes:

DR normals have a Juggle Start/Increase value of 0

DR normals have +3 added to their usual Juggle Limit

More recently, the official definitions used by Capcom are slightly different than these community-designated terms. When reading official patch notes, the following terms are used instead:

Combo Count Initial Value

Combo Count Additional Value

Combo Count Upper Limit

These are frame advantage values when the attack hits or is blocked. If the number is positive, then the move will recover before the defender can act again. If the number is negative, the defender will be able to act before the attacker and maybe even punish. KD refers to knockdown on hit, and the listed KD Advantage refers to how many frames the attacker can act before the defender finishes their wakeup animation.
Note that generally, there is an extra +2 hit advantage on Counterhits and +4 hit advantage on Punish Counters (exceptions are noted in the description).

How many frames it takes for a move to finish after the active frames have finished. For projectiles, recovery is considered to begin after the first active frame.
Moves with different recovery values on hit/block/whiff may have multiple values listed like X(Y), with specific details listed in the description.

How many frames it takes before the move becomes 'active' or have a hit box. The last startup frame and the first active frame are the same frame, meaning all values are written as Startup + 1.
Moves with multiple relevant startup values may be listed as X(Y); for example, a move that hits airborne first before hitting grounded opponents, or a 2-hit move where the first hit whiffs at some ranges.

Some moves play out an extended recovery animation when no other button/direction is input (for crouching moves, it applies when holding any down direction). These are often referred to as "actionable recovery" frames; in some games, the term IASA (Interruptible As Soon As) refers to the frame that Actionable Recovery begins.
Letting the Actionable Recovery frames play out can change the character's position, potentially setting up spacing traps by recovering farther away. For example, Manon 5HP will recover much farther away from the opponent if no input is performed immediately after her recovery; holding back or down-back to block will keep her much closer to the opponent.

Introduction

edit

A pretty, mysterious young girl who claims to travel through parallel worlds. Using a sort of crest and code, she manifests powers beyond the laws of the world. Talks like someone beyond her years.

Ingrid is a tricky zoner who likes to pester opponents around the mid-range with an array of projectiles while building up Sun Crests from afar . With enough resources, Ingrid can deal absurd damage from across the screen , but has to be careful not to be too predictable against defiant opponents.

At the mid-range, Ingrid has a fundamental zoning game. Sun Shot is a projectile that pauses briefly before traveling forward that can also be held to alter its timing against parry-happy opponents. The Light and Medium versions both shoot forward with the only difference being their initial velocity and distance before pausing, while the Heavy version shoots upward at an angle before descending. Ingrid also has Light Rising Sun as a typical anti-air with an atypical quarter-circle motion. If she has the Drive Gauge, Ingrid can combine the meterless horizontal Sun Shots with an OD angled Sun Shot and vice versa to fill the screen with obstacles. At closer ranges, Ingrid has some solid pokes to complement her Sun Shots, like 5HK's long range, 2HP's special cancels, 5HP's whiff punishes, and 4MK's target combo extensions. When she does get a hit, Rising Sun serves as her primary combo ender, with the Medium version working off lights and the Heavy version being much slower but offering a variety of follow up afterwards.

Once the opponent is far enough away, Ingrid can use Light Sun Flare to gain a Sun Crest, a buff that enhances her zoning and Super Arts to even greater heights. Ingrid can stock up to four Sun Crests at a time, and can choose between Medium Sun Flare to keep the opponent far away from Ingrid and continue stocking up, or spend up to two Crests for Heavy Sun Flare to cash out on her resources with a devastating full-screen beam. Furthermore, OD Sun Flare stacks with Sun Crests, with a 2-stock OD Sun Flare piercing across the screen as an anti-fireball, a combo extender, a long-range whiff punish, and a pressure tool all wrapped up in one. She can also perform Solar Burst, a downward-angled air variant that can snipe opponents from afar or extend from Halo Flight for a terrifying low crush.

If the opponent gets frustrated and starts trying to chase her down, Ingrid has a few extra options to take them by surprise. Vanishing Sun lets Ingrid teleport either forward with a point-black dropkick, downward with an overhead hip attack that ground bounces, or backwards to escape full-screen to get back to zoning. While they all are on the slower side, they work well in conjunction with Sun Flare, tacking on some extra damage and repositioning her up close for pressure. Finally, Sun Veil has Ingrid hold up her beloved Monoid to take a hit, sending the opponent back mid-screen if successful. While somewhat slow on its own and vulnerable to throws, OD Sun Veil removes those weaknesses entirely, giving her an invincible reversal to further frustrate the opponent.

Along with Drive Gauge and Sun Crests, Ingrid's also got some remarkable, albeit atypical Super Arts to further manage. Her Level 1 Super Art Shining Sun is a flip kick that works as a reversal, anti-air, and combo ender alike. It can be enhanced with Sun Crests to further increase its damage to a whopping 2700 for massive reward. Ingrid's Level 2 Super Art Order of the Sun summons three shooting stars to fall on the opponent, landing either in front of, on top of, or behind the opponent depending on the button strength. Ingrid can combo in and out of the shooting stars for massive damage, and can also spend Sun Crests to launch even more projectiles. Finally, her Level 3 Super Art Cosmic Ray spawns a projectile on top of the opponent, letting her tack on even more damage at the end of her juggles. Though powerful, her Super Arts tend to be a bit on the slower side, making them risky to throw out in neutral. As with most of her kit, careful resource management is required to avoid being caught off guard.

While she may be comfortable from afar and at the mid range, Ingrid has a much less pleasant time up close. Without her Sun Crests, her damage potential is drastically cut down, and opponents capable of skipping through her fireball pressure through projectile-invulnerability or alternate angles can prevent her from building up her stocks, since her Sun Shots and even her Super Art 2 disappear if she gets hit. Ingrid also lacks a naturally plus-on-block normal, forcing her to either spend resources or delay her buttons to maintain advantage. Any careless stocks, haphazard fireballs, or blocked Super Arts can lead to massive punishes, especially against eagle-eyed opponents waiting for them. In order to enforce her domain, Ingrid has to keep the opponent guessing by alternating between teleports, fireballs, pokes, and her OD Counter to avoid being predictable. Only by invoking the fear of the Goddess can she unleash divine power.

Overall, if you like abnormal zoning patterns, can get into your opponent's head, and want to cash out with absurd damage, unleash the power of the sun with Ingrid!

Pick if you like:
Avoid if you dislike:

Spacial Oddities: An array of projectiles that can be used concurrently, an anti-air with a uniquely easy input, and a full-screen beam all come together to make for a tricky zoning game.

Cataclysmic Cutie: Having HUGE burst damage when loaded up on system and character resources.

Limbs of the Forbidden One: Strong pokes and whiff punishes that lead into Target Combos and further damage.

Hey! No Fair!: Being susceptible to virtually any kind of anti-fireball tool in midrange scenarios, due to the frame data/"stop-start" nature of her Sun Shot fireball. Spin Knuckles, Shoto Tatsus, Slides– if it has a whiff of projectile-invuln, and your opponent has a pulse, they can react, and it will punish. Risk awareness is advised.

God Complex: Managing a stock system to gain access to her full potential, and having to choose between Sun Crests and okizeme.

Depressurisation: Generally having a harder time sticking close enough after buttons pressure, as well as lacking in natural plus frames to better enforce any kind of respect.
