Frame Data Tables / Hitbox Explanation - SF6

Hitbox Images

Red: Attack hitbox
Pink: Throw hitbox
Green: Hurtbox (strikes/projectiles)

Certain move properties, like Projectile Invuln or Air Invuln, may be printed onto the hurtbox and listed in the move description

A complete lack of hurtboxes represents full invulnerability

Blue: Throw hurtbox

Throw will succeed if the pink throw hitbox overlaps with the blue throwable hurtbox

Opponent must be on the ground (except for Air Throws which only target airborne opponents)

Teal: Unique/Interaction box

Applies character-specific effects when two of these hitboxes overlap

Examples: Rashid's air current, Blanka's electric moves + Blanka-chan, Guile's Sonic Blade + Sonic Boom

Purple: Armor/Counter Hitbox

Can appear on top of green hurtboxes or replace them entirely

Orange: Projectile Clash hitbox

Not a projectile itself, but interacts with and destroys projectiles of the same priority

Light Orange box on Drive Impact : represents the "cinematic DI Slowdown" interaction hitboxes

Active

How many frames a move remains active (can hurt opponents) for. For projectiles with a maximum active period, a value may be listed in [brackets], but this number is not factored into the move's total frame count.
For multi-hit moves with no gaps between the active hitboxes, active frames are listed as X,Y (or sometimes X*Y)

For multi-hit moves with gaps between hits, active frames are listed as X(n)Y where n = the frame gap between hitboxes.

Cancel

Available options for canceling one move into another move.
"Chn": Chain cancel (Light normals; specific chain options listed in Description)

"TC": Target Combo

"Sp": Special move

"SA": Super Art (if a number is listed, refers only to that specific Super; SA3 = Lv.3 Super Art)

"Jmp": Jump cancel (usually on hit only, if applicable)

"SS": Serenity Stream (Chun-Li's stance)

"PS": Prowler Stance (Alex's stance)
If one hit of a multi-hit attack is cancelable, this can be indicated with (1st), (2nd), etc.

Occasionally, a move can be canceled only into a specific follow-up (e.g. Dee Jay [4]6P > 22PP); this can be indicated by listing the move input in the Cancel field, or with an asterisk that is explained in the move notes (Sp*)

Cancel Hitconfirm Windows

Hitconfirm reaction windows into Special Moves, Target Combos, and Super Arts.
Refers to the amount of time (in frames) you have to cancel one attack into another attack on reaction
e.g. most cancelable 2MKs have a 13 frame window to cancel into a Special/Super on reaction, making them nearly impossible to hitconfirm

Counts from the first frame the attack connects until the final cancelable frame
Visual effects like hitsparks and HP drain do not actually occur until frame 2; the first frame is still counted to keep the numbers consistent with previous games, and because it is technically possible to start reacting to the character's reeling animation on frame 1

If a Target Combo is cancelable into another attack, the hitconfirm window will include the entire sequence starting from the first hit
If there is a frame gap on block between hits of the TC, the hitconfirm window may also be included for just the followup hit

Some sequences like Ken's 5MP~HP TC may have a range of values listed (43f~47f). In this example, inputting 5MP~HP at its usual timing gives a 43f hitconfirm into a Special/Super. Delaying the chain into HP gives more total time for the final hitconfirm.

Damage

Attack damage on hit. Multi-hit moves may have the damage listed for individual hits as X,Y (or sometimes X*Y). Sometimes a move's damage changes depending on which active frame connects, or on cinematic vs. non-cinematic hits; in this case, multiple values may be listed, and it will be clarified in the move description.

Damage Scaling

Some moves cause additional damage scaling in combos. Refer to Game Data page for a more detailed breakdown.
Scaling Types:

Starter: When a move begins the combo , the next attack is scaled by X percent
e.g. Ryu 2MK (20% Starter) > Hadoken: Hadoken is at 80% damage scaling

Combo: When a move is comboed into , the next attack is scaled by X percent or X number of hits
e.g. Ryu 2HP > OD High Blade Kick (2-Hit Combo Scaling) > Shoryuken: Shoryuken is at 70% damage scaling (100% > 100% > [skip 80%] > 70%)

e.g. Cammy 5HP > OD Spiral Arrow (5% Combo Scaling) > Cannon Spike: Cannon Spike is at 75% damage scaling (100% > 100% > [80-5 = 75%])

Immediate: When a move is comboed into , this attack is scaled by X percent
e.g. Drive Impact Crumple (20% Starter) > Throw (20% Immediate): Throw is at 60% damage scaling

Multiplier: A damage scaling multiplier applies after Perfect Parry (50%) and mid-combo Drive Rush (15%). Any hits in the combo continue their usual damage scaling, but reduced by these amounts. These can bring the minimum scaling below the usual 10%, and they stack with each other; as a result, the minimum scaling can reach 4% using a long Drive Rush combo after Perfect Parry.

Minimum Scaling: The lowest damage scaling that can be applied to an attack. Super Art Level 1/2/3 generally has 30%/40%/50% minimum scaling respectively. This ensures the attack will still do reasonable damage even at the end of a heavily scaled combo.

Drive Rush Cancel Advantage

Refers to the frame advantage when canceling a normal, command normal, or Target Combo into Drive Rush on hit or block (abbreviated as DRC for Drive Rush Cancel). This is calculated at the moment a follow-up attack can be input, not at the moment the character can block or perform movement options. An attack that with DRC +8 on Hit can link into an 8-frame attack, and DRC +4 on Block can create a true blockstring into a 4-frame attack.
Note that any DRC on Block worse than +4 cannot form a true blockstring, allowing the opponent to interrupt with an invincible reversal. Most light normals are slightly negative after a DRC on block, meaning the opponent can mash their fastest normal to guarantee a counter-hit (though this requires fast reactions). The attacking character could punish this with Light > DRC into an immediate invincible attack, but this would be an incredibly expensive and high-risk gambit.

Forced Knockdown

Most airborne command normals, special moves, and Super Arts put the user in a "Forced Knockdown" state. While in this state, an air knockdown will occur when being hit by any attack, even if it would otherwise cause an air reset.
As an example, Ryu's 2HP causes an air reset when used as an anti-air. Against a move like Cammy's Hooligan Combination, however, the 2HP puts her into an air knockdown state. This allows Ryu to successfully cancel 2HP into Shoryuken for a juggle, similar to how a Drive Impact wall splat works. Taking advantage of Forced Knockdown juggles is important for dealing with moves like Ken's Dragonlash, Dhalsim's Air Teleport, or Kimberly's 6HK~Hop sequence.

Moves that already cause an air knockdown, like most j.MP air-to-airs, will not display the "Forced Knockdown" message.

Guard

Refers to the direction an attack must be blocked. L is for Low attacks (must be blocked crouching), H is for High attacks/overheads (must be blocked standing), LH is for attacks that can be blocked crouching or standing. T is for Throw attacks which cannot be blocked.

Juggles

When a character is put into an Air Knockdown state, it is often possible to follow up with a Juggle attack before they hit the ground. In the simplest terms, there are 2 main juggle states:
Free Juggle: any attack can juggle, causing an Air Reset or an Air Knockdown

Limited Juggle: only specific attacks with juggle potential may juggle

The following is a more detailed overview of the SF6 juggle system:

Juggle Count (JC) : The status of the character being juggled. A high JC limits which attacks can work in juggles.

JC0: free juggle state - any attack that can hit an airborne opponent will work

JC1+: limited juggle state - juggle only works if the attack's Juggle Limit ≥ defender's Juggle Count
A juggle count of -1 represents a crumple state; this can lead to a grounded or airborne hit depending on timing

Juggle Start (JS) : When starting a juggle, the opponent's JC will be set to this value. May be different vs. standing and airborne opponents.

Attack with Juggle Start value of 3 will put opponent at JC3, so only attacks with Juggle Limit value ≥ 3 can follow up

Even for attacks that don't normally start a juggle, this is relevant for Forced Knockdown and Crumple situations

Juggle Increase (JI) : When opponent is already in a juggle state, attacks will increase the opponent's JC by this amount.

Airborne opponent at JC1 followed by attack with Juggle Increase value of 3 will set opponent to JC4

Juggle Limit (JL) : Property of an attack hitbox that determines whether it connects on a juggled opponent. The JL must be ≥ the opponent's JC to hit successfully.

An uppercut with a JL value of 5 will connect on an opponent at JC5 or below, but will whiff on JC6 opponent

Most normals have a JL value of 0, meaning they only work in Free Juggle (JC0) states

Some multi-hit attacks have different JL values on each hit, so a 3-hit move may only hit twice in juggles

An example to tie everything together:

An attack (JS3) launches opponent into the air (Opponent now at JC3)

Followed up with an attack (JI2/JL4); it connects, because JL4 ≥ JC3 (Opponent now at JC5)

Attempts to juggle again with same attack (JL4), but whiffs because JL4 < JC5 (Opponent hits the ground)

Drive Rush notes:

DR normals have a Juggle Start/Increase value of 0

DR normals have +3 added to their usual Juggle Limit

More recently, the official definitions used by Capcom are slightly different than these community-designated terms. When reading official patch notes, the following terms are used instead:

Combo Count Initial Value

Combo Count Additional Value

Combo Count Upper Limit

On Hit/Block

These are frame advantage values when the attack hits or is blocked. If the number is positive, then the move will recover before the defender can act again. If the number is negative, the defender will be able to act before the attacker and maybe even punish. KD refers to knockdown on hit, and the listed KD Advantage refers to how many frames the attacker can act before the defender finishes their wakeup animation.
Note that generally, there is an extra +2 hit advantage on Counterhits and +4 hit advantage on Punish Counters (exceptions are noted in the description).

Recovery

How many frames it takes for a move to finish after the active frames have finished. For projectiles, recovery is considered to begin after the first active frame.
Moves with different recovery values on hit/block/whiff may have multiple values listed like X(Y), with specific details listed in the description.

Startup

How many frames it takes before the move becomes 'active' or have a hit box. The last startup frame and the first active frame are the same frame, meaning all values are written as Startup + 1.
Moves with multiple relevant startup values may be listed as X(Y); for example, a move that hits airborne first before hitting grounded opponents, or a 2-hit move where the first hit whiffs at some ranges.

IASA / Actionable Recovery

Some moves play out an extended recovery animation when no other button/direction is input (for crouching moves, it applies when holding any down direction). These are often referred to as "actionable recovery" frames; in some games, the term IASA (Interruptible As Soon As) refers to the frame that Actionable Recovery begins.
Letting the Actionable Recovery frames play out can change the character's position, potentially setting up spacing traps by recovering farther away. For example, Manon 5HP will recover much farther away from the opponent if no input is performed immediately after her recovery; holding back or down-back to block will keep her much closer to the opponent.

While somewhat stubby compared to other characters, 5LK is Ingrid's longest ranged light normal, making it an important -5 punish and combo extension tool. It links after 5LP to allow light confirms when chains are too far to reach, and is the only natural link after 2MP if the opponent is standing.

5LK can be canceled into MK or OD Sun Rise to end combos depending on your desired meter usage. As a Punish Counter starter, it can combo into Enhanced or OD Sun Flare, which can lead to moderate damage despite the initial damage scaling. A 5LK punish canceled into DRC can also link into 5HK ; while this route is expensive and heavily scaled, it may help squeeze out the last bit of damage for a kill.

A cancelable poke with solid range and forward movement during startup. It serves as a middle ground between the stubby but fast 2MP and the longer but slow-whiffing 2MK in neutral. It also deals more damage than 2MP , making it the more rewarding link option when the frame data allows it.

5MK has higher hitstun than Ingrid's other cancelable mediums, allowing for a cancel to HK Sun Rise as a Punish Counter or out of Drive Rush , leading to much greater meterless damage and corner carry. If you confirm the opponent is standing, 5MK > DRC can link to 4HP ~ HP for a strong juggle anywhere on the screen.

The forward movement makes it an excellent harassment tool in the corner, especially if the opponent doesn't have invincible tools to deal with projectiles. A cancel into LP Sun Shot will interrupt most reversal normals while allowing Ingrid to maintain nearly the same spacing, forcing the opponent to find a way out. Some characters can hit a button with no hurtbox extension to trade with the fireball, but this is often range-dependent and requires quick reflexes. When not canceled, the pushback is quite high, so Ingrid cannot use 5MK as an advancing Burnout tool similar to A.K.I.'s 5MP .

A 2-hit kick that starts hitting vertically before swinging the leg downward. Very effective at breaking the armor of moves like Zangief 5[HP] or Marisa's Gladius, while easily confirming into a Super cancel if the opponent tries to anticipate it with Drive Impact . It links naturally into 5LP / 2LP from surprisingly far, and into 5MP on Counter-hit from nearly any range where both hits connect. If you score a whiff punish, it will always link to 5MK outside of fringe max-range scenarios, leading to excellent damage.

5HK is a strong approach tool out of Drive Rush , becoming +2 on Block inside throw range for a strike/throw mixup and linking to mediums on hit. The disjointed hitbox makes it difficult to interrupt at longer ranges (but note that the bottom hitbox of the 2nd hit is the only part that can actually connect in neutral — the top hitbox is combo-only).

One of the most useful properties of 5HK is its cancel into SA2 . On hit, it leads to a full combo conversion with any medium button, while in block it leaves Ingrid at the perfect advantage for a strike/throw/shimmy mixup, with all options leading to devastating damage under the right conditions. The lenient hitconfirm window also allows players to easily save their resources for a guaranteed kill.

If 5HK connects on an airborne opponent, the ground bounce allows SA1 and SA3 to juggle when canceled into. You can also activate SA2 and pick up a Sun Rise juggle, but this is height-dependent; a low connect that only juggles into LK Sun Rise may not hit the opponent into the SA2 projectiles. This is mostly applicable in juggle scenarios, as 5HK is not a very consistent anti-air.

overview.title: Street Fighter 6/Yasmine
tables:
Character breakdown in progress

Yasmine is a new character ! This page is currently under construction and information might be inaccurate, incomplete, or missing entirely.

🤝 Want to help us out? Join the SF6 Resource Hub for more info on editing and other ways you can potentially help with this resource.

Great all-around mobility, with one of the fastest-moving Drive Rushes in the game

Unique setplay tools that can create high/low, left/right, and strike/throw mixups

Easy hitconfirms with multi-hit normals and safe Target Combos for low-risk pressure

Playing almost entirely at closer ranges, with limited options to deal with strong zoners

Managing your combo routes based on whether you want to spend or preserve your Bayani Mode enhancement

A relatively stiff combo structure that suffers greatly from damage scaling

A[ L ~ L ~ L ~ L ]: 2LK ~ 2LP ~ L Daloy ng Tubig ~ L Alon
On Block: stops after 2LP

Auto-hitconfirm if opponent is hit by the 2nd light in the string

2L ~A[ 2L ~ L ~ L ~ L ~ L ]: 2LP ~ 2LK ~ 5LP ~ LP ~ M Daloy ng Tubig ~ M Alon
Variant ender that lets Yasmine get a Light Assist Combo from a chained 2LP starter

Lacks any auto-hitconfirm properties (but can be stopped safely after 4 light hits)

A[ M ~ M ~ M ~ M ~ M ~ M ]: 2MP ~ OD Daloy ng Tubig ~ SA2 ~ H Talim ng Hangin ~ 5HP(2) ~ H Lipad ng Agila
Burnout: 2MP ~ M Daloy ng Tubig ~ M Alon

On Block: stops after OD / M Daloy ng Tubig

No SA2 : stops after OD Daloy ng Tubig

A[ H ~ H ~ H ~ H ]: 5HP(2) ~ OD Talim ng Hangin ~ 5HP(2) ~ SA3
Burnout: 5HP(2) ~ M Talim ng Hangin ~ SA3

On Block: stops after OD / M Talim ng Hangin

No SA3 : ends with H Talim ng Hangin instead

5L is 5LK but switches to 5LP if chained into
This allows the use of the Kidlat na Hiwa ( 5LP ~ LP ) Target Combo

5LP is unavailable outside of chains

When Yasmine successfully hits with any version of Alon (236P~6P), Talim ng Hangin (214P), or SA1 (236236K), she enters an enhanced state called Bayani Mode that causes her karambit to glow with a blue aura. This enhancement greatly improves the properties of Alon on hit and block, and is spent whenever Alon is used (except when * OD Alon connects on Hit , in which case Yasmine will keep her power-up.

You cannot store multiple stocks of Bayani Mode ; similar to Ryu's Denjin charge, you get one use before needing to build another stock. This incentivizes using it early whenever possible, as most combo routes will naturally put you back into Bayani Mode .

While Yasmine's SA2 Install is active, her whole body glows with a blue aura, causing her to stay in Bayani Mode until the timer expires. Each use of * Alon or her install-only * 4KK special drains the timer by 25%.

After the install ends, Yasmine keeps her regular Bayani stock even if the last move depleted the install timer. If Daloy ng Tubig was activated with any time remaining on the install, the following Alon will be enhanced without spending the Bayani stock (even though you're inputting Alon after the install ends).

Bayani enhanced moves are notated with * in front of the name or input, such as * Alon, * 4KK , or 236MP ~ * 6P .
Frame Data Tables / Hitbox Explanation - SF6

Red: Attack hitbox
Pink: Throw hitbox
Green: Hurtbox (strikes/projectiles)

Certain move properties, like Projectile Invuln or Air Invuln, may be printed onto the hurtbox and listed in the move description

A complete lack of hurtboxes represents full invulnerability

Blue: Throw hurtbox

Throw will succeed if the pink throw hitbox overlaps with the blue throwable hurtbox

Opponent must be on the ground (except for Air Throws which only target airborne opponents)

Teal: Unique/Interaction box

Applies character-specific effects when two of these hitboxes overlap

Examples: Rashid's air current, Blanka's electric moves + Blanka-chan, Guile's Sonic Blade + Sonic Boom

Purple: Armor/Counter Hitbox

Can appear on top of green hurtboxes or replace them entirely

Orange: Projectile Clash hitbox

Not a projectile itself, but interacts with and destroys projectiles of the same priority

Light Orange box on Drive Impact : represents the "cinematic DI Slowdown" interaction hitboxes

How many frames a move remains active (can hurt opponents) for. For projectiles with a maximum active period, a value may be listed in [brackets], but this number is not factored into the move's total frame count.
For multi-hit moves with no gaps between the active hitboxes, active frames are listed as X,Y (or sometimes X*Y)

For multi-hit moves with gaps between hits, active frames are listed as X(n)Y where n = the frame gap between hitboxes.

Available options for canceling one move into another move.
"Chn": Chain cancel (Light normals; specific chain options listed in Description)

"TC": Target Combo

"Sp": Special move

"SA": Super Art (if a number is listed, refers only to that specific Super; SA3 = Lv.3 Super Art)

"Jmp": Jump cancel (usually on hit only, if applicable)

"SS": Serenity Stream (Chun-Li's stance)

"PS": Prowler Stance (Alex's stance)
If one hit of a multi-hit attack is cancelable, this can be indicated with (1st), (2nd), etc.

Occasionally, a move can be canceled only into a specific follow-up (e.g. Dee Jay [4]6P > 22PP); this can be indicated by listing the move input in the Cancel field, or with an asterisk that is explained in the move notes (Sp*)

Hitconfirm reaction windows into Special Moves, Target Combos, and Super Arts.
Refers to the amount of time (in frames) you have to cancel one attack into another attack on reaction
e.g. most cancelable 2MKs have a 13 frame window to cancel into a Special/Super on reaction, making them nearly impossible to hitconfirm

Counts from the first frame the attack connects until the final cancelable frame
Visual effects like hitsparks and HP drain do not actually occur until frame 2; the first frame is still counted to keep the numbers consistent with previous games, and because it is technically possible to start reacting to the character's reeling animation on frame 1

If a Target Combo is cancelable into another attack, the hitconfirm window will include the entire sequence starting from the first hit
If there is a frame gap on block between hits of the TC, the hitconfirm window may also be included for just the followup hit

Some sequences like Ken's 5MP~HP TC may have a range of values listed (43f~47f). In this example, inputting 5MP~HP at its usual timing gives a 43f hitconfirm into a Special/Super. Delaying the chain into HP gives more total time for the final hitconfirm.

Attack damage on hit. Multi-hit moves may have the damage listed for individual hits as X,Y (or sometimes X*Y). Sometimes a move's damage changes depending on which active frame connects, or on cinematic vs. non-cinematic hits; in this case, multiple values may be listed, and it will be clarified in the move description.

Some moves cause additional damage scaling in combos. Refer to Game Data page for a more detailed breakdown.
Scaling Types:

Starter: When a move begins the combo , the next attack is scaled by X percent
e.g. Ryu 2MK (20% Starter) > Hadoken: Hadoken is at 80% damage scaling

Combo: When a move is comboed into , the next attack is scaled by X percent or X number of hits
e.g. Ryu 2HP > OD High Blade Kick (2-Hit Combo Scaling) > Shoryuken: Shoryuken is at 70% damage scaling (100% > 100% > [skip 80%] > 70%)

e.g. Cammy 5HP > OD Spiral Arrow (5% Combo Scaling) > Cannon Spike: Cannon Spike is at 75% damage scaling (100% > 100% > [80-5 = 75%])

Immediate: When a move is comboed into , this attack is scaled by X percent
e.g. Drive Impact Crumple (20% Starter) > Throw (20% Immediate): Throw is at 60% damage scaling

Multiplier: A damage scaling multiplier applies after Perfect Parry (50%) and mid-combo Drive Rush (15%). Any hits in the combo continue their usual damage scaling, but reduced by these amounts. These can bring the minimum scaling below the usual 10%, and they stack with each other; as a result, the minimum scaling can reach 4% using a long Drive Rush combo after Perfect Parry.

Minimum Scaling: The lowest damage scaling that can be applied to an attack. Super Art Level 1/2/3 generally has 30%/40%/50% minimum scaling respectively. This ensures the attack will still do reasonable damage even at the end of a heavily scaled combo.

Refers to the frame advantage when canceling a normal, command normal, or Target Combo into Drive Rush on hit or block (abbreviated as DRC for Drive Rush Cancel). This is calculated at the moment a follow-up attack can be input, not at the moment the character can block or perform movement options. An attack that with DRC +8 on Hit can link into an 8-frame attack, and DRC +4 on Block can create a true blockstring into a 4-frame attack.
Note that any DRC on Block worse than +4 cannot form a true blockstring, allowing the opponent to interrupt with an invincible reversal. Most light normals are slightly negative after a DRC on block, meaning the opponent can mash their fastest normal to guarantee a counter-hit (though this requires fast reactions). The attacking character could punish this with Light > DRC into an immediate invincible attack, but this would be an incredibly expensive and high-risk gambit.

Most airborne command normals, special moves, and Super Arts put the user in a "Forced Knockdown" state. While in this state, an air knockdown will occur when being hit by any attack, even if it would otherwise cause an air reset.
As an example, Ryu's 2HP causes an air reset when used as an anti-air. Against a move like Cammy's Hooligan Combination, however, the 2HP puts her into an air knockdown state. This allows Ryu to successfully cancel 2HP into Shoryuken for a juggle, similar to how a Drive Impact wall splat works. Taking advantage of Forced Knockdown juggles is important for dealing with moves like Ken's Dragonlash, Dhalsim's Air Teleport, or Kimberly's 6HK~Hop sequence.

Moves that already cause an air knockdown, like most j.MP air-to-airs, will not display the "Forced Knockdown" message.

Refers to the direction an attack must be blocked. L is for Low attacks (must be blocked crouching), H is for High attacks/overheads (must be blocked standing), LH is for attacks that can be blocked crouching or standing. T is for Throw attacks which cannot be blocked.

When a character is put into an Air Knockdown state, it is often possible to follow up with a Juggle attack before they hit the ground. In the simplest terms, there are 2 main juggle states:
Free Juggle: any attack can juggle, causing an Air Reset or an Air Knockdown

Limited Juggle: only specific attacks with juggle potential may juggle

The following is a more detailed overview of the SF6 juggle system:

Juggle Count (JC) : The status of the character being juggled. A high JC limits which attacks can work in juggles.

JC0: free juggle state - any attack that can hit an airborne opponent will work

JC1+: limited juggle state - juggle only works if the attack's Juggle Limit ≥ defender's Juggle Count
A juggle count of -1 represents a crumple state; this can lead to a grounded or airborne hit depending on timing

Juggle Start (JS) : When starting a juggle, the opponent's JC will be set to this value. May be different vs. standing and airborne opponents.

Attack with Juggle Start value of 3 will put opponent at JC3, so only attacks with Juggle Limit value ≥ 3 can follow up

Even for attacks that don't normally start a juggle, this is relevant for Forced Knockdown and Crumple situations

Juggle Increase (JI) : When opponent is already in a juggle state, attacks will increase the opponent's JC by this amount.

Airborne opponent at JC1 followed by attack with Juggle Increase value of 3 will set opponent to JC4

Juggle Limit (JL) : Property of an attack hitbox that determines whether it connects on a juggled opponent. The JL must be ≥ the opponent's JC to hit successfully.

An uppercut with a JL value of 5 will connect on an opponent at JC5 or below, but will whiff on JC6 opponent

Most normals have a JL value of 0, meaning they only work in Free Juggle (JC0) states

Some multi-hit attacks have different JL values on each hit, so a 3-hit move may only hit twice in juggles

An example to tie everything together:

An attack (JS3) launches opponent into the air (Opponent now at JC3)

Followed up with an attack (JI2/JL4); it connects, because JL4 ≥ JC3 (Opponent now at JC5)

Attempts to juggle again with same attack (JL4), but whiffs because JL4 < JC5 (Opponent hits the ground)

Drive Rush notes:

DR normals have a Juggle Start/Increase value of 0

DR normals have +3 added to their usual Juggle Limit

More recently, the official definitions used by Capcom are slightly different than these community-designated terms. When reading official patch notes, the following terms are used instead:

Combo Count Initial Value

Combo Count Additional Value

Combo Count Upper Limit

These are frame advantage values when the attack hits or is blocked. If the number is positive, then the move will recover before the defender can act again. If the number is negative, the defender will be able to act before the attacker and maybe even punish. KD refers to knockdown on hit, and the listed KD Advantage refers to how many frames the attacker can act before the defender finishes their wakeup animation.
Note that generally, there is an extra +2 hit advantage on Counterhits and +4 hit advantage on Punish Counters (exceptions are noted in the description).

How many frames it takes for a move to finish after the active frames have finished. For projectiles, recovery is considered to begin after the first active frame.
Moves with different recovery values on hit/block/whiff may have multiple values listed like X(Y), with specific details listed in the description.

How many frames it takes before the move becomes 'active' or have a hit box. The last startup frame and the first active frame are the same frame, meaning all values are written as Startup + 1.
Moves with multiple relevant startup values may be listed as X(Y); for example, a move that hits airborne first before hitting grounded opponents, or a 2-hit move where the first hit whiffs at some ranges.

Some moves play out an extended recovery animation when no other button/direction is input (for crouching moves, it applies when holding any down direction). These are often referred to as "actionable recovery" frames; in some games, the term IASA (Interruptible As Soon As) refers to the frame that Actionable Recovery begins.
Letting the Actionable Recovery frames play out can change the character's position, potentially setting up spacing traps by recovering farther away. For example, Manon 5HP will recover much farther away from the opponent if no input is performed immediately after her recovery; holding back or down-back to block will keep her much closer to the opponent.

Introduction

edit

A high-schooler who became a fighter to find her lost brother. She is a shy and gentle soul, but beams with confidence in fights, where she uses her Lolo's moves.

As the first Filipino Street Fighter, Yasmine zips onto the scene with blindingly high speed and relentless close quarters mixups. Boasting a lightning fast drive rush, good walk speed, a plethora of forward advancing normals and body projectile specials, a boomerang projectile that creates setups, and a wide variety of way to generate safe combo enders, Yasmine is a dizzyingly aggressive close quarters fighter.

[st HP, cr LK, safe on block body projectile, etc]

And mixups you will have to enact, because her damage is some of the worst in the game. Many of Yasmine's normals and target combos have scaling, and her bread-and-butter routing go into specials that add even more. Her Demon Raid leap and boomerang are useful tools, but in addition to being slow and vulnerable (especially compared to the wide cast of shotos) they aggressively scale when starting combos too. She suffers from weak medium ranges and awkward conversions , forcing her back into her forward-advancing moves, which in a kit as straightforward as hers can feel limiting and constrained.

Don't let that scare you though -- Yasmine is an easy to pick up character who can stick her opponent in a blender of terrifying aggression. If you want to rep the Philippines with pride, take her for a spin and see how holding a karambit feels.

Kaya mo ‘yan!

Pick if you like:
Avoid if you dislike:

Great all-around mobility, with one of the fastest-moving Drive Rushes in the game

Unique setplay tools that can create high/low, left/right, and strike/throw mixups

Easy hitconfirms with multi-hit normals and safe Target Combos for low-risk pressure

Playing almost entirely at closer ranges, with limited options to deal with strong zoners

Managing your combo routes based on whether you want to spend or preserve your Bayani Mode enhancement

A relatively stiff combo structure that suffers greatly from damage scaling

Bayani Mode

edit

When Yasmine successfully hits with any version of Alon (236P~6P), Talim ng Hangin (214P), or SA1 (236236K), she enters an enhanced state called Bayani Mode that causes her karambit to glow with a blue aura. This enhancement greatly improves the properties of Alon on hit and block, and is spent whenever Alon is used (except when * OD Alon connects on Hit , in which case Yasmine will keep her power-up.

You cannot store multiple stocks of Bayani Mode ; similar to Ryu's Denjin charge, you get one use before needing to build another stock. This incentivizes using it early whenever possible, as most combo routes will naturally put you back into Bayani Mode .

While Yasmine's SA2 Install is active, her whole body glows with a blue aura, causing her to stay in Bayani Mode until the timer expires. Each use of * Alon or her install-only * 4KK special drains the timer by 25%.

After the install ends, Yasmine keeps her regular Bayani stock even if the last move depleted the install timer. If Daloy ng Tubig was activated with any time remaining on the install, the following Alon will be enhanced without spending the Bayani stock (even though you're inputting Alon after the install ends).

Bayani enhanced moves are notated with * in front of the name or input, such as * Alon, * 4KK , or 236MP ~ * 6P .

Frame Data Tables / Hitbox Explanation - SF6

Hitbox Images

Red: Attack hitbox
Pink: Throw hitbox
Green: Hurtbox (strikes/projectiles)

Certain move properties, like Projectile Invuln or Air Invuln, may be printed onto the hurtbox and listed in the move description

A complete lack of hurtboxes represents full invulnerability

Blue: Throw hurtbox

Throw will succeed if the pink throw hitbox overlaps with the blue throwable hurtbox

Opponent must be on the ground (except for Air Throws which only target airborne opponents)

Teal: Unique/Interaction box

Applies character-specific effects when two of these hitboxes overlap

Examples: Rashid's air current, Blanka's electric moves + Blanka-chan, Guile's Sonic Blade + Sonic Boom

Purple: Armor/Counter Hitbox

Can appear on top of green hurtboxes or replace them entirely

Orange: Projectile Clash hitbox

Not a projectile itself, but interacts with and destroys projectiles of the same priority

Light Orange box on Drive Impact : represents the "cinematic DI Slowdown" interaction hitboxes

Active

How many frames a move remains active (can hurt opponents) for. For projectiles with a maximum active period, a value may be listed in [brackets], but this number is not factored into the move's total frame count.
For multi-hit moves with no gaps between the active hitboxes, active frames are listed as X,Y (or sometimes X*Y)

For multi-hit moves with gaps between hits, active frames are listed as X(n)Y where n = the frame gap between hitboxes.

Cancel

Available options for canceling one move into another move.
"Chn": Chain cancel (Light normals; specific chain options listed in Description)

"TC": Target Combo

"Sp": Special move

"SA": Super Art (if a number is listed, refers only to that specific Super; SA3 = Lv.3 Super Art)

"Jmp": Jump cancel (usually on hit only, if applicable)

"SS": Serenity Stream (Chun-Li's stance)

"PS": Prowler Stance (Alex's stance)
If one hit of a multi-hit attack is cancelable, this can be indicated with (1st), (2nd), etc.

Occasionally, a move can be canceled only into a specific follow-up (e.g. Dee Jay [4]6P > 22PP); this can be indicated by listing the move input in the Cancel field, or with an asterisk that is explained in the move notes (Sp*)

Cancel Hitconfirm Windows

Hitconfirm reaction windows into Special Moves, Target Combos, and Super Arts.
Refers to the amount of time (in frames) you have to cancel one attack into another attack on reaction
e.g. most cancelable 2MKs have a 13 frame window to cancel into a Special/Super on reaction, making them nearly impossible to hitconfirm

Counts from the first frame the attack connects until the final cancelable frame
Visual effects like hitsparks and HP drain do not actually occur until frame 2; the first frame is still counted to keep the numbers consistent with previous games, and because it is technically possible to start reacting to the character's reeling animation on frame 1

If a Target Combo is cancelable into another attack, the hitconfirm window will include the entire sequence starting from the first hit
If there is a frame gap on block between hits of the TC, the hitconfirm window may also be included for just the followup hit

Some sequences like Ken's 5MP~HP TC may have a range of values listed (43f~47f). In this example, inputting 5MP~HP at its usual timing gives a 43f hitconfirm into a Special/Super. Delaying the chain into HP gives more total time for the final hitconfirm.

Damage

Attack damage on hit. Multi-hit moves may have the damage listed for individual hits as X,Y (or sometimes X*Y). Sometimes a move's damage changes depending on which active frame connects, or on cinematic vs. non-cinematic hits; in this case, multiple values may be listed, and it will be clarified in the move description.

Damage Scaling

Some moves cause additional damage scaling in combos. Refer to Game Data page for a more detailed breakdown.
Scaling Types:

Starter: When a move begins the combo , the next attack is scaled by X percent
e.g. Ryu 2MK (20% Starter) > Hadoken: Hadoken is at 80% damage scaling

Combo: When a move is comboed into , the next attack is scaled by X percent or X number of hits
e.g. Ryu 2HP > OD High Blade Kick (2-Hit Combo Scaling) > Shoryuken: Shoryuken is at 70% damage scaling (100% > 100% > [skip 80%] > 70%)

e.g. Cammy 5HP > OD Spiral Arrow (5% Combo Scaling) > Cannon Spike: Cannon Spike is at 75% damage scaling (100% > 100% > [80-5 = 75%])

Immediate: When a move is comboed into , this attack is scaled by X percent
e.g. Drive Impact Crumple (20% Starter) > Throw (20% Immediate): Throw is at 60% damage scaling

Multiplier: A damage scaling multiplier applies after Perfect Parry (50%) and mid-combo Drive Rush (15%). Any hits in the combo continue their usual damage scaling, but reduced by these amounts. These can bring the minimum scaling below the usual 10%, and they stack with each other; as a result, the minimum scaling can reach 4% using a long Drive Rush combo after Perfect Parry.

Minimum Scaling: The lowest damage scaling that can be applied to an attack. Super Art Level 1/2/3 generally has 30%/40%/50% minimum scaling respectively. This ensures the attack will still do reasonable damage even at the end of a heavily scaled combo.

Drive Rush Cancel Advantage

Refers to the frame advantage when canceling a normal, command normal, or Target Combo into Drive Rush on hit or block (abbreviated as DRC for Drive Rush Cancel). This is calculated at the moment a follow-up attack can be input, not at the moment the character can block or perform movement options. An attack that with DRC +8 on Hit can link into an 8-frame attack, and DRC +4 on Block can create a true blockstring into a 4-frame attack.
Note that any DRC on Block worse than +4 cannot form a true blockstring, allowing the opponent to interrupt with an invincible reversal. Most light normals are slightly negative after a DRC on block, meaning the opponent can mash their fastest normal to guarantee a counter-hit (though this requires fast reactions). The attacking character could punish this with Light > DRC into an immediate invincible attack, but this would be an incredibly expensive and high-risk gambit.

Forced Knockdown

Most airborne command normals, special moves, and Super Arts put the user in a "Forced Knockdown" state. While in this state, an air knockdown will occur when being hit by any attack, even if it would otherwise cause an air reset.
As an example, Ryu's 2HP causes an air reset when used as an anti-air. Against a move like Cammy's Hooligan Combination, however, the 2HP puts her into an air knockdown state. This allows Ryu to successfully cancel 2HP into Shoryuken for a juggle, similar to how a Drive Impact wall splat works. Taking advantage of Forced Knockdown juggles is important for dealing with moves like Ken's Dragonlash, Dhalsim's Air Teleport, or Kimberly's 6HK~Hop sequence.

Moves that already cause an air knockdown, like most j.MP air-to-airs, will not display the "Forced Knockdown" message.

Guard

Refers to the direction an attack must be blocked. L is for Low attacks (must be blocked crouching), H is for High attacks/overheads (must be blocked standing), LH is for attacks that can be blocked crouching or standing. T is for Throw attacks which cannot be blocked.

Juggles

When a character is put into an Air Knockdown state, it is often possible to follow up with a Juggle attack before they hit the ground. In the simplest terms, there are 2 main juggle states:
Free Juggle: any attack can juggle, causing an Air Reset or an Air Knockdown

Limited Juggle: only specific attacks with juggle potential may juggle

Attack with Juggle Start value of 3 will put opponent at JC3, so only attacks with Juggle Limit value ≥ 3 can follow up

Even for attacks that don't normally start a juggle, this is relevant for Forced Knockdown and Crumple situations

Juggle Increase (JI) : When opponent is already in a juggle state, attacks will increase the opponent's JC by this amount.

Airborne opponent at JC1 followed by attack with Juggle Increase value of 3 will set opponent to JC4

Juggle Limit (JL) : Property of an attack hitbox that determines whether it connects on a juggled opponent. The JL must be ≥ the opponent's JC to hit successfully.

An uppercut with a JL value of 5 will connect on an opponent at JC5 or below, but will whiff on JC6 opponent

Some multi-hit attacks have different JL values on each hit, so a 3-hit move may only hit twice in juggles

An attack (JS3) launches opponent into the air (Opponent now at JC3)

Followed up with an attack (JI2/JL4); it connects, because JL4 ≥ JC3 (Opponent now at JC5)

Attempts to juggle again with same attack (JL4), but whiffs because JL4 < JC5 (Opponent hits the ground)

DR normals have +3 added to their usual Juggle Limit

A combo starter with 2 hits for easy hitconfirms into the 5MP ~ MP Target Combo. The range is very short, equivalent to 5LP ; the 2nd hit actually has shorter range, but the suction effect of the 1st hit combined with the extended combo-only hitbox ensures it will always connect. This short range makes it ineffective in many +6 combo routes, like DR~ 5HP or a spaced Counter-hit light; it's most effective when used as a raw confirm tool.

When used out of Drive Rush , Yasmine gets slight advantage on block, but is outside throw range and cannot push a true strike/throw mixup; on hit, 5MP can link to itself or into 2MP for extra damage. However, it's a fairly weak Drive Rush pressure starter, as Yasmine loses her forward momentum almost immediately; approaching with DR~ 2MP is better in every way.

If the 1st hit of 5MP is Perfect Parried, Yasmine is Drive Impact punishable as she cannot cancel the rest of the animation. This makes it significantly riskier as a meaty option or as a frame trap in pressure strings, like after DR~ 2LP . Since 2MP is more rewarding on Counter-hit and lacks this weakness, it's a safer option in these scenarios.

A versatile 3-hit attack with excellent range and utility in neutral, combos, and juggles. The hitbox lacks any disjoint so it can be Counter-hit by most opposing buttons, but the effective range makes it risky for most characters to throw out a preemptive normal; whiffing at this range gives Yasmine an easy whiff punish opportunity.

5HP is safe on block, and becomes advantageous with Drive Rush or Burnout for easy pressure. DR~ 5HP will connect from around 2/3 screen (or farther if slightly delayed) and links consistently into 5MP / 2MP on hit. These links also work in most whiff punish scenarios, but the pushback prevents any follow-up links on Counter-hit .

While 5HP has a long hitconfirm window, the late cancel frames have reduced combo potential. Single-hit confirms should always be canceled into LP / OD Daloy, HK DP , or Supers , as other options are not guaranteed. This also applies to Drive Rush cancels; luckily, 2MP is usually the optimal combo extender and is guaranteed to work even on a delayed cancel (though it will no longer be a frame trap on block).

The juggle potential on 5HP is extremely high for a normal attack, and will work in practically any scenario where the startup and range allow it. This lets Yasmine pick up juggles where her 623K/ SA1 would not otherwise reach, or where the slower startup of 236PP / SA3 would not combo. The 5HP itself adds to the juggle counter, however, which makes it impossible to juggle into a meterless Daloy unless starting with a free juggle. It also adds very little damage to the overall combo, as the first 2 hits only deal 400 damage before the cancel while increasing the combo's damage scaling. Some examples of situations where 5HP can be juggled into are:

HP Talim (vs. airborne), OD Talim

HP Daloy ~ * Alon

5MP ~ MP > MP Daloy ~ * Alon

22P Boomerang (returning hit)

4KK ( SA2 )

Much like 5MP , the opponent can land a Drive Impact punish if they Perfect Parry either of the first 2 hits. Relying too heavily on DR~ 5HP without mixing in Low and Throw pressure can lead to a devastating loss of health and Drive gauge if the opponent is aware of this fact.

A forward-moving hopkick that can easily be spaced for safety, making it a great tool for chipping at the opponent's Drive gauge. Much like 5MK , it effectively counters low pokes in neutral; while it takes longer for 5HK to become a Low Crush, the entire foot hurtbox is invincible rather than just the front foot.

Landing a Low Crush or a whiff punish results in a launching Punish Counter , which can be followed up with OD Talim or DR~ 2HP anywhere on screen; at closer ranges you can also juggle into MP Talim or OD Daloy ~ Alon . The punish is significantly scaled, so it's not always worth dumping resources into the punish except to secure better screen position or enter Bayani Mode .

Combined with her fast Drive Rush speed, Yasmine can start pressure from midrange that is difficult to check on reaction, leading to tick throws or 2MP frame traps. Yasmine frequently finds herself at (like after DR~ 5HP or some Flip follow-ups), after which only 2LP can Counter-hit the opponent's reversal 4-frame button. When this happens, a reaction link into 2MP is the most consistent follow-up, as the pushback frequently causes 5MP to whiff.

With meaty timing, 2LP can be up to +6 oH / +1 oB, giving Yasmine stronger pressure or a meterless combo into mediums.

Requires SA2 install; each use consumes 375f (25%) of SA2 install timer; deals Drive Damage on normal hit (0.5 bars if both hits connect); reaches fullscreen and extends a huge proximity guard hitbox from frame 15 onward; if the 1st hit is blocked, parried, or absorbed by armor, Yasmine stops her forward movement and does not perform the 2nd hit (this hit has 2f active + 24f recovery); on hit, Yasmine will dash behind the opponent (even in the corner) and perform a 2nd hit that launches the opponent into a limited juggle state; this cross-up hit can also occur if the first hit whiffs (like in a knockdown setup or on a jumping opponent); cross-up hit has functionally 30f startup when used as an oki tool; can be canceled into from 2MK~HK and 5MK~MK~HK Target Combos on hit; active frame distribution is 2(11)5 when both hits connect; whiff recovery is 1f faster (19f) if Yasmine passes far behind the opponent before the 2nd hit comes out; startup time can be up to 3f faster (19f) if Yasmine passes through a close range airborne/teleporting opponent with no collision box; after a corner sideswitch, some follow-up juggles can whiff under the opponent (623HK requires delay, while 623MK and SA1 are auto-timed)

Cinematic time regenerates ~2.2 Drive bars for Yasmine; can be used against projectiles from about round-start distance if it catches an extended hurtbox; tall hitbox can anti-air at long range but whiffs under close/mid range opponents; leaves Yasmine fullscreen on hit even if the opponent was cornered; can still get oki with Drive Rush into a delayed normal but cannot get into throw range; 2f startup when canceled from specials or 5HP

Available at 25% HP or below; cinematic time regenerates ~2.3 Drive bars for Yasmine; can be used against projectiles from about round-start distance if it catches an extended hurtbox; tall hitbox can anti-air at long range but whiffs under close/mid range opponents; gives +1 oki after forward dash near the edge of throw range (opponent can back walk to avoid Throw or a chain after 2LK); can also Drive Rush for stronger pressure and bait 6f reversals with DR~2LP; 2f startup when canceled from specials or 5HP
"I've been practicing this a lot! Gotcha! Cool, right?"; Yasmine attacks with a kick while catching the knife; gives a shorter knockdown on Punish Counter
"I'm starving... Oh, I almost forgot! Aha! Want some? Really? Your loss! Alright, ready to go!"

"Watch this! Haaaaaaaahhhhhh! HADOKEN - Aaahhh! Wait, I did it? I gotta practice more!"; must be holding a button on frame 275 of startup to fill Yasmine with aura, causing her to perform a short-range stationary projectile attack
"Hoy! You're not taking this seriously! Underestimate me and I'll make a big meanie face like this, then I'll walk all over you! Don't sandbag me!"

overview.title: Street Fighter 6/Arjun
tables:
Character breakdown in progress

Arjun is a new character ! This page is currently under construction and information might be inaccurate, incomplete, or missing entirely.

🤝 Want to help us out? Join the SF6 Resource Hub for more info on editing and other ways you can potentially help with this resource.
Frame Data Tables / Hitbox Explanation - SF6

Red: Attack hitbox
Pink: Throw hitbox
Green: Hurtbox (strikes/projectiles)

Certain move properties, like Projectile Invuln or Air Invuln, may be printed onto the hurtbox and listed in the move description

A complete lack of hurtboxes represents full invulnerability

Blue: Throw hurtbox

Throw will succeed if the pink throw hitbox overlaps with the blue throwable hurtbox

Opponent must be on the ground (except for Air Throws which only target airborne opponents)

Teal: Unique/Interaction box

Applies character-specific effects when two of these hitboxes overlap

Examples: Rashid's air current, Blanka's electric moves + Blanka-chan, Guile's Sonic Blade + Sonic Boom

Purple: Armor/Counter Hitbox

Can appear on top of green hurtboxes or replace them entirely

Orange: Projectile Clash hitbox

Not a projectile itself, but interacts with and destroys projectiles of the same priority

Light Orange box on Drive Impact : represents the "cinematic DI Slowdown" interaction hitboxes

How many frames a move remains active (can hurt opponents) for. For projectiles with a maximum active period, a value may be listed in [brackets], but this number is not factored into the move's total frame count.
For multi-hit moves with no gaps between the active hitboxes, active frames are listed as X,Y (or sometimes X*Y)

For multi-hit moves with gaps between hits, active frames are listed as X(n)Y where n = the frame gap between hitboxes.

Available options for canceling one move into another move.
"Chn": Chain cancel (Light normals; specific chain options listed in Description)

"TC": Target Combo

"Sp": Special move

"SA": Super Art (if a number is listed, refers only to that specific Super; SA3 = Lv.3 Super Art)

"Jmp": Jump cancel (usually on hit only, if applicable)

"SS": Serenity Stream (Chun-Li's stance)

"PS": Prowler Stance (Alex's stance)
If one hit of a multi-hit attack is cancelable, this can be indicated with (1st), (2nd), etc.

Occasionally, a move can be canceled only into a specific follow-up (e.g. Dee Jay [4]6P > 22PP); this can be indicated by listing the move input in the Cancel field, or with an asterisk that is explained in the move notes (Sp*)

Hitconfirm reaction windows into Special Moves, Target Combos, and Super Arts.
Refers to the amount of time (in frames) you have to cancel one attack into another attack on reaction
e.g. most cancelable 2MKs have a 13 frame window to cancel into a Special/Super on reaction, making them nearly impossible to hitconfirm

Counts from the first frame the attack connects until the final cancelable frame
Visual effects like hitsparks and HP drain do not actually occur until frame 2; the first frame is still counted to keep the numbers consistent with previous games, and because it is technically possible to start reacting to the character's reeling animation on frame 1

If a Target Combo is cancelable into another attack, the hitconfirm window will include the entire sequence starting from the first hit
If there is a frame gap on block between hits of the TC, the hitconfirm window may also be included for just the followup hit

Some sequences like Ken's 5MP~HP TC may have a range of values listed (43f~47f). In this example, inputting 5MP~HP at its usual timing gives a 43f hitconfirm into a Special/Super. Delaying the chain into HP gives more total time for the final hitconfirm.

Attack damage on hit. Multi-hit moves may have the damage listed for individual hits as X,Y (or sometimes X*Y). Sometimes a move's damage changes depending on which active frame connects, or on cinematic vs. non-cinematic hits; in this case, multiple values may be listed, and it will be clarified in the move description.

Some moves cause additional damage scaling in combos. Refer to Game Data page for a more detailed breakdown.
Scaling Types:

Starter: When a move begins the combo , the next attack is scaled by X percent
